definition_en: to put money into a bank or account, money paid as a first part, or material laid down by water
core_image: 一枚硬币落进铁盒，盒底已经有薄薄一层
scene: 房东数完钱，把一张收据推过来，说钥匙可以拿了。 She deposited the money and kept the receipt.
sceneCN: 这里 deposit 指「存入」（第 1 个义项：把钱放进银行或账户）；句意是她把钱存进去并保留了收据。

senses.title: Put money in for keeping
senses.definition: to put money into a bank or an account
senses.definitionCN: 把钱放进银行或账户
senses.example: She deposited the money and kept the receipt.
senses.exampleCN: 她把钱存进去并保留了收据。
senses.why: Money put down in a safe place is money set apart from the pocket.
senses.whyCN: 放进安全地方的钱，就是与口袋分开的钱。

senses.title: Money paid as a first part
senses.definition: money paid first as a promise or a security
senses.definitionCN: 先付的一笔作为承诺或担保的钱
senses.example: They paid a deposit on the flat.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为这套公寓付了押金。
senses.why: A deposit says the promise has weight.
senses.whyCN: 押金是在说，这个承诺有分量。

senses.title: Material laid down by water
senses.definition: material that water or wind leaves in a layer
senses.definitionCN: 水或风留下的一层物质
senses.example: The river left a deposit of sand at the bend.
senses.exampleCN: 河流在转弯处留下一层沙。
senses.why: Water carries what it cannot hold, and sets it down.
senses.whyCN: 水搬不动的东西，就放下来。

intro.en: Deposit comes from Latin depositum, a thing placed down, from deponere, built on ponere, to place.
intro.cn: deposit 来自拉丁语 depositum（放下之物），源头是 deponere，词基为 ponere（放置）。

items.en: Deponere joined de-, meaning down, with ponere, to place.
items.cn: deponere 由 de-（向下）与 ponere（放置）合成。

items.en: Depositum named a thing placed down or entrusted.
items.cn: depositum 指放下或托付之物。

items.en: English used deposit for money placed with a bank.
items.cn: 英语用 deposit 指存进银行的钱。

items.en: Science borrowed it for layers laid down by water.
items.cn: 科学借它指水留下的层状物。

items.en: Now it covers savings, security payments and sediment.
items.cn: 如今它覆盖储蓄、担保付款与沉积物。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the deposit stem, and the meaning group moves from saving money to leaving matter behind.
note.cn: 形近组共用 deposit 词干，近义组则从存钱走到留下物质。

entries.definition: a person who puts money in a bank
entries.definitionCN: 把钱存进银行的人

entries.definition: the laying down of material, or a sworn statement
entries.definitionCN: 物质的沉积，或经宣誓的证词

entries.definition: a place where things are stored
entries.definitionCN: 存放物品的地方

entries.definition: to keep money instead of spending it
entries.definitionCN: 把钱留着而不花掉

entries.definition: a serious promise, or something given as security
entries.definitionCN: 郑重的承诺，或作为担保交出之物

entries.definition: solid matter that settles in liquid
entries.definitionCN: 沉在液体底部的固体物质

normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一枚硬币落进铁盒开始，落到河流留下的沙。

normal.en: A deposit on a flat is a promise with a price.

normal.en: A river deposits what it is too tired to carry.

normal.en: The same word works in a bank and on a river bank.
normal.cn: 同一个词，在银行与河岸都管用。

abstract.cn: 想象一只手把硬币投进投币口。

abstract.en: Picture a receipt folded once and put in a pocket.
abstract.cn: 想象一张收据被折一下，塞进口袋。

abstract.en: Picture a thin line of sand along a river bend.
abstract.cn: 想象河湾边上薄薄的一道沙。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 deposit 记成「放到底」：de 是向下，pos 是放，把钱放到底下的安全处，就是存入与押金。

root: 来自拉丁语 depositum，源头是 deponere，由 de-（向下）与 ponere（放置）组成。它先指放下或托付之物，十六世纪进入英语指存进银行的钱，十七世纪科学又借它指水留下的沉积层。

sensesIntro.en: From money laid in a safe place, to money laid down as a promise, to sand laid down by a river.
sensesIntro.cn: 从放进安全处的钱，到作为承诺交出的钱，再到河流放下的沙。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coin falls into a tin that already has a thin layer in it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚硬币落进盒底已有一层薄薄东西的铁盒。

branches.en: The first sense is money placed where it will wait.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是把钱放在一个会等你的地方。

branches.en: The second sense is money placed as proof of a promise.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是作为承诺凭据放下的钱。

branches.en: The third sense is matter placed by water and forgotten.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是水放下并被遗忘的物质。

branches.en: In a bank and in a landlord's hand, money is put down for later.
branches.cn: 在银行与房东手里，钱都是为了以后而放下。

branches.en: Both a pledge and a sandbank are things left in place.
branches.cn: 承诺的凭据与沙洲，都是留在原处的东西。

intro.en: Deposit grows a family about placing, storing and laying down, from the person to the place.
intro.cn: deposit 长出一族表示放置、储存与沉积的词，从人到地方都有。

latinIntro.en: The base is ponere, to place, with de- meaning down; posit is the same root seen in position.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是 ponere（放置），de- 表示向下；posit 这个部分也出现在 position 里。

definition_zh: 贫穷；贫困；缺乏钱财与基本生活资源的状态；也指某种东西的匮乏或贫瘠
definition_en: the state of being extremely poor, lacking the money and resources needed for basic living; also a general scarcity or barrenness
core_image: 一只空碗放在缺了角的桌上，窗外的田里只长着稀疏的草，屋里屋外都显出「不够」
scene: 救济站里的登记表写满了名字，很多人连过冬的煤都买不起。 The charity works to reduce poverty among families in the river valley.
sceneCN: 此处指「缺乏钱财与基本生活资源的状态」（第 1 个义项：缺钱维持基本生活）；句意为这家慈善机构致力于减轻河谷家庭的贫困。图中可辨识物件：空碗、破桌、稀疏的田草、救济登记表；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 贫穷；贫困（缺乏基本生活资源的状态）
匮乏；贫瘠（某种东西数量少或质量差）

forms.label: 复数（罕见，指多种贫困状况）

senses.title: Lack of money for basic needs
senses.definition: the condition of not having enough money to pay for food, shelter, clothing and health care
senses.definitionCN: 没有足够的钱支付食物、住房、衣着与医疗
senses.example: Half the village lives in poverty and often skips meals.
senses.exampleCN: 村里一半人生活在贫困中，常常省掉饭食。
senses.why: The word names a shortage of the means of living, so its core sense is money that does not stretch to necessities.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是维生手段的短缺，因此核心义就是钱不足以覆盖基本需要。

senses.title: The state of being poor
senses.definition: the ongoing social condition of being poor, with its insecurity and limited choices
senses.definitionCN: 长期处于贫穷的社会状态，伴随不安全与选择受限
senses.example: Poverty traps families in unsafe housing and unstable work.
senses.exampleCN: 贫困把家庭困在不安全的住房与不稳定的工作里。
senses.why: Poverty is not only a moment of shortage but a condition that persists and shapes a life.
senses.whyCN: 贫困不只是一时的短缺，而是一种持续并塑造生活的状态。

senses.title: Officially measured deprivation
senses.definition: the level of deprivation defined by income falling below a government or research threshold
senses.definitionCN: 以收入低于政府或研究机构设定的门槛来界定的匮乏程度
senses.example: The census reports poverty by counting households below the threshold.
senses.exampleCN: 人口普查通过统计低于门槛的家庭来报告贫困。
senses.why: Modern states turned an old condition into a number by drawing a line and counting who falls under it.
senses.whyCN: 现代国家画一条线、数清线下人数，把古老的处境变成了数字。

senses.title: Scarcity of a resource
senses.definition: a serious shortage of something needed, such as water, soil nutrients or energy
senses.definitionCN: 水、土壤养分或能源等必需品严重不足
senses.example: Poverty of rainfall kept the fields bare for months.
senses.exampleCN: 降雨稀少让田地空了好几个月。
senses.why: The idea of having too little extends from money to any resource, which gives the word its scarcity sense.
senses.whyCN: 「拥有的太少」这一想法从钱扩展到任何资源，于是有了短缺义。

senses.title: Barrenness or poor quality
senses.definition: the state of land or material being thin, worn out or lacking richness
senses.definitionCN: 土地或材料稀薄、耗竭、缺乏肥力的状态
senses.example: The poverty of the soil forced farmers to move every few years.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤贫瘠迫使农民每隔几年就迁移。
senses.why: Land that yields little looks poor in the same way a person with little money does, so the word describes thinness of quality.
senses.whyCN: 产出很少的土地，看起来就像缺钱的人一样「穷」，于是这个词也描述质地的贫薄。

senses.title: Lack of ideas or imagination
senses.definition: the quality of being unoriginal, thin or lacking intellectual substance
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏创意、内容单薄、思想贫乏的性质
senses.example: Critics attacked the poverty of the plan's imagination.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者抨击这份计划想象力的贫乏。
senses.why: If a field can be poor, so can an argument, and the metaphor of thinness carries over to thought.
senses.whyCN: 田地可以贫瘠，论证也可以，贫薄这个比喻就延伸到思想上。

senses.title: Voluntary humility in religious writing
senses.titleCN: 宗教写作中自愿的谦卑
senses.definition: the deliberate giving up of worldly wealth or self-importance, especially in religious tradition
senses.definitionCN: 尤其在宗教传统中，主动放弃世俗财富或自我重要感
senses.example: Monks took a vow of poverty and owned nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 修士立下守贫之愿，不拥有任何财物。
senses.why: Religious tradition reframed lack as a virtue when it is chosen, so poverty gained a voluntary, spiritual sense.
senses.whyCN: 宗教传统把自愿的缺乏重新解释为美德，于是贫困获得了自愿的、精神性的义项。

senses.title: Destitution and dependence on charity
senses.definition: the extreme end of poverty in which a person depends on begging or public relief to survive
senses.definitionCN: 贫困的极端一端，人靠乞讨或公共救济才能活下去
senses.example: The old poorhouse sheltered people reduced to poverty.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的济贫院收容陷入赤贫的人。
senses.why: At its worst the condition leaves a person with nothing to sell but labour or appeal, and this is the destitution sense.
senses.whyCN: 到最严重时，人除了劳力或求助已无物可售，这就是赤贫义。

intro.en: Poverty comes from Latin paupertas, the abstract noun of pauper 'poor', through Old French. The deeper origin of pauper is not established. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 该词经古法语来自拉丁语 paupertas，即 pauper「贫穷」的抽象名词。pauper 的更早来源未查明。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pauper meant 'poor, needy'. Its deeper origin is not established; the old link to a root meaning 'produce little' is a hypothesis.
items.cn: pauper 意为「贫穷、匮乏」。其更深来源无定论；把它与表示「产出很少」的词根相联系的旧说只是假说。

items.en: Paupertas 'poverty, want' was the abstract noun, and it passed into Old French as poverte.
items.cn: paupertas「贫穷、匮乏」是对应的抽象名词，后来变成古法语的 poverte。

items.en: Old French poverte entered English in the thirteenth century, naming both the condition and the lack of goods.
items.cn: 古法语 poverte 于十三世纪进入英语，既指贫穷状态，也指物品的匮乏。

items.en: Religious writing used poverty of spirit for voluntary humility, a sense that survives in set phrases.
items.cn: 宗教文献用「精神上的贫穷」指自愿的谦卑，这一义项保留在固定说法里。

items.en: From the nineteenth century poverty became an object of social measurement, defined by income against a line.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，贫穷成为社会测量对象，以收入是否低于某条线来界定。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Latin origin of pauper): no agreed Indo-European etymology exists, and the date of the abstract noun is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（pauper 的拉丁语之前来源）：没有公认的印欧语词源，抽象名词的年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close but come from other roots; group two holds words for hardship and shortage.
note.cn: 第一组是形近或音近却另有词源的词；第二组是表示困苦与短缺的词。

entries.definition: Property comes from Latin proprietas 'ownership', built on proprius 'one's own'; it has nothing to do with pauper.
entries.definitionCN: 财产来自拉丁 proprietas「所有权」，出自 proprius「自己的」，与 pauper 毫无关系。

entries.definition: Propriety also goes back to proprius and means correctness of behaviour, not lack of money.
entries.definitionCN: 礼节同样出自 proprius，指行为得体，与缺钱无关。

entries.definition: Paucity means a small number or amount and comes from Latin paucus 'few'; it is a near neighbour in meaning but not in root.
entries.definitionCN: 少量来自拉丁 paucus「少」，意思相近，词根却不同。

entries.definition: Poor is the everyday adjective related to poverty, but it comes through Old French povre from the same Latin pauper.
entries.definitionCN: poor 是与贫穷相关的日常形容词，经古法语 povre 来自同一个拉丁 pauper。

entries.definition: Destitution is poverty so severe that a person lacks food, shelter and any means of recovery.
entries.definitionCN: 赤贫是严重到缺乏食物、住所与任何恢复手段的贫困。

entries.definition: Deprivation stresses the absence of specific necessities such as heating, food or schooling.
entries.definitionCN: 匮乏强调取暖、食物或教育等具体必需品的缺失。

entries.definition: Hardship is suffering caused by difficult conditions, which may occur without absolute poverty.
entries.definitionCN: 困苦是艰难处境带来的痛苦，未必达到绝对贫困。

entries.definition: Scarcity is a short supply of a particular resource and is the general form of the resource sense.
entries.definitionCN: 稀缺指某种资源供应不足，是资源义的一般化形式。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin base, real relatives and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: The Latin base means poor, and the abstract ending turns it into the state of being poor.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根意为贫穷，抽象后缀把它变成「贫穷的状态」。

normal.en: The everyday adjective and the formal noun belong to the same family.
normal.cn: 日常形容词与正式名词属于同一词族。

normal.en: Fixed phrases carry the measured sense: poverty line, relative poverty, extreme poverty.
normal.cn: 固定说法承载测量义：贫困线、相对贫困、极端贫困。

normal.en: The same word can describe thin soil or a thin argument, because both are forms of not having enough.
normal.cn: 同一个词既能形容贫瘠的土壤，也能形容单薄的论证，因为两者都是「不够」。

normal.en: Religious tradition added the voluntary sense: a vow of poverty is a choice, not a misfortune.
normal.cn: 宗教传统加上自愿义：守贫之愿是选择，而非不幸。

abstract.en: Picture a bowl that is always half empty, however often it is filled.
abstract.cn: 想象一只碗，无论添多少次，总有一半是空的。

abstract.en: Picture a field that grows grass but never grain.
abstract.cn: 想象一块地只长草，从不结粮。

abstract.en: Picture a room full of furniture and still somehow bare.
abstract.cn: 想象一间堆满家具却仍显得空荡的屋子。

examples.en: The programme cut poverty among older people by raising the basic pension.
examples.cn: 该项目通过提高基本养老金减少了老年人的贫困。

examples.en: Poverty of data made the report's conclusions uncertain.
examples.cn: 数据的匮乏让报告的结论难以确定。

examples.en: She took a vow of poverty and gave away her inheritance.
examples.cn: 她立下守贫之愿，把继承的财产捐了出去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破屋」——屋顶漏风、米缸见底，就是贫穷；记住「破」与「贫」的连带感

root: 拉丁 pauper「贫穷」经古法语进入英语，加上抽象名词后缀构成 paupertas「贫穷、匮乏」，再演变为今天的贫穷一词；pauper 的拉丁语之前来源不确定，相关词根联系多为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one shortage: money is missing, then the condition persists, is counted, is extended to resources, to soil, to thought, to chosen humility and finally to total destitution.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种「短缺」展开：先是缺钱，继而状态持续、被计数，再扩展到资源、土壤、思想、自愿的谦卑，最后到一无所有。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty bowl on a broken table, with thin grass outside and an empty coal sack by the door.
core.cn: 核心意象：缺角桌上的空碗，窗外稀疏的草，门边空着的煤袋。

branches.en: THE SHORTAGE ITSELF: money is missing, and the lack settles into a lasting condition.
branches.cn: 短缺本身：钱不够，而且这种缺乏沉淀为持久状态。

branches.en: THE COUNT: a line is drawn and the condition becomes an official number.
branches.cn: 计数：画一条线，处境就变成官方数字。

branches.en: FROM MONEY TO MATERIAL: the same thinness describes a scarce resource and barren soil.
branches.cn: 从钱到物：同一种「薄」也能形容短缺的资源与贫瘠的土壤。

branches.en: THIN THOUGHT: an argument can be as poor as a field.
branches.cn: 单薄的思想：论证可以像田地一样贫瘠。

branches.en: CHOSEN AND TOTAL LACK: lack becomes a vow at one end and destitution at the other.
branches.cn: 自愿的与彻底的缺乏：一端是守贫之愿，另一端是赤贫。

intro.en: Poverty is a Latin abstract noun that grew a wide metaphorical reach in English, from money to soil to ideas.
intro.cn: 贫穷是一个拉丁抽象名词，在英语里长出了很宽的比喻范围，从金钱到土壤再到思想。

latinIntro.en: Pauper and paupertas supply the core; English added the adjective, the verb and several compounds.
latinIntro.cn: pauper 与 paupertas 提供核心，英语再加形容词、动词与若干复合词。

items.example: Poverty kept the family in one room.
items.exampleCN: 贫穷让这家人挤在一个房间。
最贫困的家庭缺少取暖。

items.meaning: in a poor way; also unwell
items.exampleCN: 这家诊所物资供应很差。
债务使整个城区陷入贫困。

items.example: The soil was impoverished by years of planting.
Impoverishment followed the closure of the mine.
items.exampleCN: 矿井关闭后出现了贫困化。

items.example: Aid reached the poverty-stricken villages late.
items.exampleCN: 援助很晚才到达饱受贫困之苦的村庄。

items.example: A paucity of evidence weakened the case.

definition_en: following the usual and accepted way of doing things
core_image: 一整排相同的窗子，尺寸和间距都一样
scene: 邻居都装同样的白窗帘，只有她挂了一块彩布。 Her house stands out among the conventional ones.
sceneCN: 这里 conventional 指「传统的」（第 1 个义项：按多数人接受的方式行事）；句意是她的房子在那些传统样式的房子中格外显眼。

senses.title: Following custom
senses.definition: acting in the way most people in a society accept
senses.definitionCN: 按社会多数人接受的方式行事
senses.example: They chose a conventional name for the baby.
senses.exampleCN: 他们给宝宝取了个传统的名字。
senses.why: A well-worn path is easy to walk, and easy to notice.
senses.whyCN: 走熟的路好走，也容易被人看见。

senses.title: Usual in method
senses.definition: standard rather than special or new
senses.definitionCN: 采取标准做法而非特殊或新颖的做法
senses.example: The farm uses conventional tools.
senses.exampleCN: 这个农场使用常规工具。
senses.why: Most work is done with what has already been tested.
senses.whyCN: 多数活儿是用已经验过的东西干的。

senses.title: Lacking surprise
senses.definition: plain and not unusual, sometimes in a dull way
senses.definitionCN: 普通、毫不特别，有时显得乏味
senses.example: The ending was too conventional to remember.
senses.exampleCN: 这个结尾太落套，让人记不住。
senses.why: A picture that copies every other picture leaves no mark.
senses.whyCN: 一张照抄其他画的画，不会留下痕迹。

intro.en: Conventional is convention plus the adjective ending -al, from Latin convenire, to come together and agree.
intro.cn: conventional 是 convention 加形容词词尾 -al 构成，源头是拉丁语 convenire（走到一起并取得一致）。

items.en: Convenire meant to meet and to agree.
items.cn: convenire 意为会面并取得一致。

items.en: Conventio named the agreement that followed a meeting.
items.cn: conventio 指会面之后达成的约定。

items.en: French convention carried the sense of an accepted custom.
items.cn: 法语 convention 带有被接受的习俗之义。

items.en: English convention meant a settled habit of a group.
items.cn: 英语 convention 指群体固定的习惯。

items.en: The adjective conventional grew to mean following that habit.
items.cn: 形容词 conventional 逐渐指依照这种习惯。

items.en: It now also hints at a lack of freshness.
items.cn: 如今它也暗示缺少新意。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin coming base ven-, and the meaning group names other words for what follows the usual path.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的来词基 ven-，近义组列出其他表示循常规的词。

entries.definition: an accepted habit or a large meeting
entries.definitionCN: 惯例；大会

entries.definition: in the accepted way
entries.definitionCN: 按惯例地

entries.definition: not following the usual way
entries.definitionCN: 非常规的

entries.definition: following older customs
entries.definitionCN: 传统的

entries.definition: normal and not special
entries.definitionCN: 普通的；平常的

entries.definition: used as the usual accepted model
entries.definitionCN: 标准的

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a well-worn path, then move to tested tools and to a picture that copies every other picture.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从走熟的路开始，再到验过的工具，最后到照抄别的画的那幅画。

normal.en: Conventional is the adjective of convention: it follows the accepted way.
normal.cn: conventional 是 convention 的形容词：它照着被接受的方式走。

normal.en: A row of identical windows is convention in stone.
normal.cn: 一排一模一样的窗子，是石头做成的惯例。

normal.en: Conventional wisdom is what everyone says before thinking.
normal.cn: 传统看法是大家还没想就都会说的话。

normal.en: The word can praise safety or blame dullness.
normal.cn: 这个词既能夸稳妥，也能怪乏味。

normal.en: Same path, same steps, same result.
normal.cn: 同一条路，同样的步子，同样的结果。

abstract.en: Picture ten houses with the same white front.
abstract.cn: 想象十座房子有着同样的白色门面。

abstract.en: Picture a row of tools worn smooth by years.
abstract.cn: 想象一排被岁月磨得光滑的工具。

abstract.en: Picture a painting copied line for line from another.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅画逐线照抄了另一幅。

examples.en: She prefers conventional clothes at work.
examples.cn: 上班时她更喜欢传统样式的衣服。

examples.en: The farmers still use conventional methods.
examples.cn: 这些农民仍使用常规方法。

examples.en: His solution was clever but conventional.
examples.cn: 他的办法聪明却很落套。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 conventional 记成 convention（惯例）加 al（形容词尾）：凡事照着惯例走，就是传统的、常规的。

root: 由 convention（惯例、约定）加形容词词尾 -al 构成，源头是拉丁语 convenire（走到一起并取得一致），指循惯例、合常规与缺少新意。

sensesIntro.en: From walking a well-worn path, to using tested tools, and at last to copying a picture already seen.
sensesIntro.cn: 从走一条熟路，到使用验过的工具，最后到照抄一幅已经看过的画。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: ten houses sharing one white front.
core.cn: 核心意象：十座房子共用一个白色门面。

branches.en: The first sense simply follows what people accept.
branches.cn: 第一个义项只是照着人们接受的做法。

branches.en: The second sense chooses the standard tool.
branches.cn: 第二个义项选用标准的工具。

branches.en: The third sense notices what the habit costs.
branches.cn: 第三个义项看出这种习惯付出的代价。

branches.en: Custom and standard method are close neighbours.
branches.cn: 习俗与标准方法是一对近邻。

branches.en: A tested way can also become a dull one.
branches.cn: 验过的路，也可能变成乏味的路。

intro.en: Conventional is convention plus the adjective ending -al.
intro.cn: conventional 由 convention 加形容词词尾 -al 构成。

latinIntro.en: The coming base ven- also appears in convention, convene and prevent.
latinIntro.cn: 来词基 ven- 也出现在 convention、convene 与 prevent 中。

items.exampleCN: 他走了一条不寻常的路。

items.meaning: to bring people into one meeting
a usual practice of a group

definition_zh: 谈判；协商；议价；通过（弯道、障碍）；（票据）兑现
definition_en: the process of discussing something in order to reach an agreement, or the successful passing of a difficult route or a financial instrument
core_image: 两个人隔桌而坐，桌上摊着一张纸，各自把笔移到中间那条线的两侧。
scene: 两家公司在会议室里逐条修改合同，先把价格放一边。 They began a long negotiation over delivery dates.
sceneCN: 这里 negotiation 是“为达成协议而进行的谈判”（第 1 个义项）；句意：他们开始就交货日期进行长时间的谈判；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 谈判；协商；议价；（弯道、障碍的）通过；（票据的）兑现、转让

derivatives.zh: 谈判；协商；通过（险处）；兑现（票据）

senses.title: Talk aimed at agreement
senses.definition: the process of discussion between parties who want an agreement but do not yet share the same terms
senses.definitionCN: 希望达成协议但条件尚未一致的各方向进行讨论的过程
senses.example: The negotiation lasted three days before both sides signed.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判持续了三天，双方才签字。
senses.why: The word names the whole process, not one offer: parties move positions until a text can be accepted by both.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是整个过程，而不是某一次报价：各方不断移动立场，直到出现双方都能接受的文本。

senses.title: Bargaining over price and terms
senses.titleCN: 议价磋商：一项一项地换条件
senses.definition: bargaining in which price, quantity, delivery, or other terms are traded against each other
senses.definitionCN: 就价格、数量、交货或其他条款相互交换让步的讨价还价
senses.example: The price was settled in a separate negotiation over volume discounts.
senses.exampleCN: 价格在另一场关于批量折扣的议价中确定。
senses.why: Commerce turns agreement into a trade of terms: one side gives on price, the other gives on time, and the sum must still balance.
senses.whyCN: 商业把协议变成条款交换：一方在价格上让步，另一方在时间上让步，总和仍须平衡。

senses.title: Diplomatic bargaining
senses.titleCN: 外交谈判：国家之间的文字较量
senses.definition: formal talks between states or political groups, often over conflict, borders, or treaties
senses.definitionCN: 国家或政治集团之间就冲突、边界或条约进行的正式会谈
senses.example: The peace negotiation produced a ceasefire but no final border.
senses.exampleCN: 和平谈判带来了停火，却没有确定最终边界。
senses.why: When the parties are states, the same process carries public authority: what is agreed becomes a document that binds populations, not just signers.
senses.whyCN: 当各方是国家时，同一过程带有公共权威：谈成的内容会成为约束民众而不仅是签字者的文件。

senses.title: Dealing over work and pay
senses.titleCN: 合同薪酬谈判：把自己的条件摆上桌
senses.definition: talks between an employer and an employee or union about wages, hours, and working conditions
senses.definitionCN: 雇主与雇员或工会就工资、工时与劳动条件进行的会谈
senses.example: Her salary negotiation gained a raise and an extra week of leave.
senses.exampleCN: 她的薪酬谈判争取到了加薪和额外一周假期。
senses.why: Here the abstract process becomes personal: the terms being traded are the conditions of one's daily life, so preparation and timing matter.
senses.whyCN: 这里抽象过程变得切身：被交换的条款是一个人日常生活的条件，因此准备与时机都很重要。

senses.title: Getting a vehicle round a bend
senses.titleCN: 过弯：把车身稳稳带过弯道
senses.definition: the act of steering or driving a vehicle safely through a curve or narrow passage
senses.definitionCN: 操纵车辆安全通过弯道或狭窄路段的行为
senses.example: The bus slowed for the sharp negotiation of the mountain road.
senses.exampleCN: 大巴减速以通过山路的急弯。
senses.why: From 'dealing with a difficulty' comes the physical sense: the driver negotiates the curve as a rider negotiates a rough path.
senses.whyCN: 从“应对困难”引申出物理义：司机把车稳稳带过弯道，就像骑手带马穿过一段崎岖小路。

senses.title: Passing an obstacle
senses.titleCN: 越过险处：从障碍中穿过去
senses.definition: the successful passing of a physical obstruction, such as a fence, a reef, or rough ground
senses.definitionCN: 成功穿过栅栏、暗礁或崎岖地面等物理障碍
senses.example: The boat's negotiation of the reef took all the crew's attention.
senses.exampleCN: 船只穿越暗礁的过程让全体船员全神贯注。
senses.why: The sense keeps the core idea of dealing with something difficult, but the difficulty is now ground or water rather than another person.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项保留“应对难事”的核心意思，但难事从“另一个人”变成了地面或水面。

senses.title: Cashing or transferring an instrument
senses.titleCN: 票据兑现：让一张纸变成钱
senses.definition: the passing of a cheque, bill, or other financial instrument through the banking system so that it is paid or transferred
senses.definitionCN: 让支票、汇票等金融票据经银行系统完成付款或转让
senses.example: The negotiation of the cheque failed because the signature did not match.
senses.exampleCN: 这张支票因签名不符而未能兑现。
senses.why: A financial instrument must also be 'carried through' a system; the old commercial sense of negotiation survives in banking as the successful passage of paper.
senses.whyCN: 金融票据也必须“穿过”一套系统；negotiation 古老的商业义项在银行领域以“票据顺利通过”的形式留存下来。

senses.title: Agreeing on what words mean
senses.titleCN: 意义协商：边说边确认对方懂了
senses.definition: the interactive process by which speakers adjust wording until both understand a meaning in the same way
senses.definitionCN: 说话者调整措辞，直到双方以相同方式理解某一含义的互动过程
senses.example: In the language class, the negotiation of meaning happened through gestures and repetition.
senses.exampleCN: 在语言课上，意义协商通过手势和重复完成。
senses.why: Even without a contract, two minds must reach a shared version of what a word refers to; that temporary agreement is a negotiation too.
senses.whyCN: 即使没有合同，两个头脑也必须就一个词指什么达成共同版本；这种临时一致同样是一场谈判。

intro.en: Negotiation comes from Latin negotiatio, business or trade, from negotiari, to do business, and negotium, a matter of business. Its literal makeup is 'not leisure'.
intro.cn: negotiation 来自拉丁语 negotiatio“生意、交易”，出自动词 negotiari“做买卖”与名词 negotium“事务、业务”。其字面构成是“不闲暇”。

items.en: Otium meant leisure, ease, or time free from public affairs. It is the peaceful half of the word's ancestry.
items.cn: otium 意为闲暇、安逸，或免于公共事务的时间；它是这个词祖先中安静的那一半。

items.en: Negotium joined nec- 'not' to otium: not-leisure, hence business, employment, and a matter requiring effort.
items.cn: negotium 把 nec-“不”与 otium 结合：不闲暇，因而指业务、职务，以及需要费力的事务。

items.en: The verb meant to carry on business, to trade, and also to transact or manage a matter.
items.cn: 该动词意为做买卖、从事交易，也指经办或处理一桩事务。

items.en: The noun named business, traffic in goods, and the conduct of a transaction. It did not yet mean formal talks.
items.cn: 该名词指生意、货物交易以及交易的处理，当时还没有“正式会谈”的意思。

items.en: French narrowed the word toward the talks that precede a transaction, and English borrowed that sense in the 16th century.
items.cn: 法语把词义收窄到交易之前的商谈，英语在 16 世纪借入了这一含义。

items.en: Diplomacy, labour relations, and banking each kept a branch: talks, bargaining, and the passing of an instrument through a system.
items.cn: 外交、劳资关系与银行各自保留了一条分支：会谈、议价，以及票据在系统中的通过。

note.en: The first group is the negotiate family; the second compares ways of settling a difference, from friendly talk to third-party decision.
note.cn: 第一组是 negotiate 词族；第二组比较解决分歧的方式，从友好商谈到第三方裁决。

entries.definition: to discuss in order to agree, or to get past a difficulty. It names the action.
entries.definitionCN: 为达成一致而商谈，或越过困难；命名的是动作。

entries.definition: a person who takes part in talks on behalf of a side. It names the actor, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 代表一方参加谈判的人；命名的是行动者，不是过程。

entries.definition: open to being changed by agreement, or able to be transferred as payment. It describes a quality of terms.
entries.definitionCN: 可经协商改变的，或可作为支付转让的；描述条款的性质。

entries.definition: hard trading of offers, especially over price. It sounds more competitive than negotiation.
entries.definitionCN: 围绕报价的强硬交换，尤指价格；比 negotiation 更有竞争味。

entries.definition: help from a neutral third party to reach agreement. The parties still decide, but someone else runs the talk.
entries.definitionCN: 由中立第三方协助达成协议；仍由当事方决定，但谈话由他人主持。

entries.definition: settlement by an outside judge whose decision binds the parties. It replaces negotiation with a ruling.
entries.definitionCN: 由外部裁决者作出有约束力的决定；以裁决取代谈判。

entries.definition: asking for opinions before deciding. It gathers views but does not require agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 决定前征求意见；收集看法，但不要求达成一致。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: nec- 'not' plus otium 'leisure'. Business is literally not-leisure, and negotiation is the talk that business requires.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：nec-“不”加 otium“闲暇”。业务字面上就是“不闲暇”，而 negotiation 是业务所需的商谈。

normal.en: Not-leisure: the moment people stop relaxing and start trading terms.
normal.cn: 不闲暇：人们停止放松、开始交换条件的那一刻。

normal.en: A negotiation is a table with two pens and one text between them.
normal.cn: 谈判就是一张桌子、两支笔，以及中间那一份文本。

normal.en: In banking, negotiation is paper passing through a system; in driving, it is a car passing through a curve.
normal.cn: 在银行，negotiation 是票据穿过系统；在驾驶，是车穿过弯道。

normal.en: Salary negotiation trades hours of your life for a number on a contract.
normal.cn: 薪酬谈判用你生命中的小时数换合同上的一个数字。

normal.en: Language learners negotiate meaning with gestures before they find the word.
normal.cn: 语言学习者先用手势协商意义，然后才找到那个词。

abstract.en: Negotiation begins only where two sides are both dependent and unwilling to lose the other.
abstract.cn: 谈判只始于双方既相互依赖、又不愿失去对方的地方。

abstract.en: The word's ancestry says business is the absence of leisure; the modern noun says agreement is the absence of easy silence.
abstract.cn: 这个词的祖先说业务是闲暇的缺席；现代名词则说协议是轻松沉默的缺席。

abstract.en: To negotiate a bend is to accept that the path will not be straight; every agreement has a curve built into it.
abstract.cn: 把车带过一个弯道，就是接受道路不会笔直；每份协议里都内置了一道弯。

examples.en: The union entered negotiations with a single demand: a fixed schedule two weeks in advance.
examples.cn: 工会带着一项诉求进入谈判：提前两周给出固定排班。

examples.en: Years of practice let the old driver negotiate the narrow bridge without slowing much.
examples.cn: 多年练习让老司机几乎不减速就通过了那座窄桥。

examples.en: The cheque failed negotiation because the account had been closed.
examples.cn: 这张支票未能兑现，因为账户已经销户。

dict_mnemonic.text: nego（不）+ tiation（歇）——不歇着，坐下来谈条件，就是谈判。

root: 源自拉丁语 negotiatio（生意、交易），出自 negotium（事务、业务），字面为 nec-“不”+ otium“闲暇”，即“不闲暇之事”；后经法语收窄为“交易前的商谈”，再扩展出外交、劳资、过弯与票据兑现等义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of negotiation. The core is always a difficult passage made manageable: two sides pass from disagreement to agreement, a driver passes a curve, a cheque passes through a bank, or two speakers pass into shared meaning.
sensesIntro.cn: negotiation 的八个义项，核心始终是“让一段难走的路变得可走”：双方从分歧走到一致，司机通过弯道，支票穿过银行系统，两个说话者进入共同理解。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people at a table, one sheet of paper, and each pen moving toward the middle line.
core.cn: 核心意象：两人隔桌，一张纸，两支笔各自向中间那条线移动。

chain: FRENCH NEGOCIATION TALKS BEFORE A DEAL
ENGLISH NEGOTIATION THE PROCESS OF REACHING TERMS

branches.en: MAKING A DEAL: the general process and the item-by-item trade of price and terms.
branches.cn: 达成交易：一般谈判过程，与逐项交换价格和条款的议价。

branches.en: TALKS WITH WEIGHT: state-to-state diplomacy and employer-to-employee bargaining.
branches.cn: 有分量的会谈：国家对国家的外交，与雇主对雇员的劳资谈判。

branches.en: PHYSICAL PASSAGE: steering through a bend and passing a reef or rough ground.
branches.cn: 物理通过：驾车过弯，以及穿过暗礁或崎岖地面。

branches.en: FINANCIAL PASSAGE: a cheque or bill carried through the banking system.
branches.cn: 金融通过：支票或汇票经银行系统完成流转。

branches.en: SHARED MEANING: speakers adjusting words until both mean the same thing.
branches.cn: 共享意义：说话者调整措辞，直到双方所指相同。

intro.en: Negotiation is negotiate plus -ion, the action-noun suffix. The family adds -or for the person, -able for what can be traded or changed, and re- for doing it again.
intro.cn: negotiation 是 negotiate 加 -ion（动作名词后缀）。词族用 -or 表示人，-able 表示可交易或可更改，re- 表示重新进行。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is otium, leisure, negated by nec-. Negotium and negotiari are the business words built on that negation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基是 otium“闲暇”，由 nec- 否定。negotium 与 negotiari 就是建立在这一否定之上的业务用语。

items.meaning: leisure, ease, freedom from public business
items.meaningCN: 闲暇；安逸；免于公共事务
items.example: Otium in Roman life meant time for letters and thought.
items.exampleCN: 在罗马生活中，otium 指用于写信与思考的时间。

items.meaning: to discuss for agreement, or to get past a difficulty
items.meaningCN: 为达成协议而商谈，或越过困难
items.example: They negotiated the price down by ten percent.
items.exampleCN: 他们把价格谈低了百分之十。

items.meaning: the process of bargaining or passing a difficulty
items.meaningCN: 谈判过程，或通过困难的过程
items.example: The negotiation produced a draft both sides could sign.
items.exampleCN: 谈判产生了一份双方都能签署的草案。

items.example: The chief negotiator asked for a short break.
items.exampleCN: 首席谈判代表要求短暂休息。

items.meaning: open to agreement, or legally transferable
items.meaningCN: 可协商的，或可依法转让的
items.example: The delivery date is still negotiable.
The landlord agreed to renegotiate the lease.
items.exampleCN: 房东同意重新协商租约。

items.meaning: a merchant or dealer, now rare
items.example: The old records list him as a negotiant in silk.
items.exampleCN: 旧档案把他记为丝绸商人。

items.meaning: settled by talks rather than by rule
items.meaningCN: 经谈判议定的，而非按规定定的
items.example: The workers returned under a negotiated settlement.
items.exampleCN: 工人们在谈判达成的解决方案下复工。

definition_zh: 直的；笔直的；正直的；直接地
definition_en: not bent or curved, honest and direct, or in a direct way

definition_zh: 反应；回应；化学反应；反对
definition_en: a response to something that happens; a chemical change; opposition to a change or idea; an adverse bodily response
core_image: 投入水中的钠块剧烈翻腾
scene: 一小块钠落进水里，立刻嘶嘶作响、四处窜动。 Her first reaction was to laugh.
sceneCN: 这里 reaction 是「反应」（第 1 个义项：对刺激的回应）；句意为她的第一反应是大笑。画面里可留意：水中翻腾的钠块、四溅的水花、笑声。

pos.zh: 反应；回应；化学反应；反对

senses.title: A response
senses.definition: a response in feeling, speech or action to something that happens
senses.definitionCN: 对发生之事在情感、言语或行动上的回应
senses.example: Her first reaction was to laugh.
senses.exampleCN: 她的第一反应是大笑。
senses.why: Reaction is the noun of react, so it names the acting back that follows some earlier event.
senses.whyCN: reaction 是 react 的名词，因此它命名的是在先发生之事之后「回过来的行动」。

senses.title: A chemical change
senses.definition: a process in which substances combine or break down and form new substances
senses.definitionCN: 物质结合或分解、生成新物质的过程
senses.example: The experiment produced a bright chemical reaction.
senses.exampleCN: 这个实验产生了明亮的化学反应。
senses.why: Chemistry uses the same noun for substances acting on one another and being changed in return.
senses.whyCN: 化学用同一个名词指物质彼此作用、并因此改变。

senses.title: Opposition to change
senses.definition: a movement or feeling that resists a change, often a political or social one
senses.definitionCN: 抵制某种改变的运动或情绪，常指政治或社会变革
senses.example: The reform met with strong reaction from conservative groups.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革遭到保守团体的强烈反对。
senses.why: When the acting back is turned against a new force, reaction means resistance rather than mere response.
senses.whyCN: 当回过来的行动转而对抗一股新力量时，reaction 便指抵抗，而不只是回应。

senses.title: An adverse bodily response
senses.definition: a harmful or unwanted response of the body to a drug or substance
senses.definitionCN: 身体对药物或物质的有害或不良回应
senses.example: The patient had an allergic reaction to the drug.
senses.exampleCN: 病人对药物产生了过敏反应。
senses.why: A body that reacts badly to a substance produces what medicine calls a reaction, a response that harms rather than helps.
senses.whyCN: 身体对某物质反应不良，就产生医学所称的 reaction，一种有害而无益的回应。

intro.en: Reaction is react plus the Latin noun ending -ion; react itself goes back to Latin reagere, to act back.
intro.cn: reaction 是 react 加拉丁名词词尾 -ion；react 本身可追溯到拉丁语 reagere（回过来行动）。

items.en: Agere meant to do or drive, and action is the noun of that doing.
items.cn: agere 意为做或驱动，action 就是这一动作的名词。

items.en: Reagere meant to act back, and English react kept that picture of a return of force.
items.cn: reagere 意为回过来行动，英语 react 保留了力量回返的画面。

items.en: The Latin ending -ion turned the verb into a noun, giving English reaction as the name of the return act.
items.cn: 拉丁词尾 -ion 把动词变成名词，给英语带来 reaction，作为这一回返动作的名称。

items.en: Chemists adopted the noun for substances that act on one another and are transformed.
items.cn: 化学家采用这个名词，指彼此作用并发生转变的物质。

items.en: Modern English uses reaction for responses of all kinds, chemical change, political resistance and bodily responses to drugs.
items.cn: 现代英语用 reaction 指各种回应、化学变化、政治抵制，以及身体对药物的反应。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on react; the near-meaning group gathers words for responses and resistance.
note.cn: 形近组收由 react 构成的形式；近义组收表示回应与抵抗的词。

definition_zh: 账户；账目；叙述；解释；占比；赊账；（商业）客户
definition_en: a record or arrangement for money, a spoken or written report, or a reason given for something
core_image: 柜台上一本摊开的账簿，每一行都记着谁欠谁多少
scene: 月底对账时，她把每一笔进出都念给丈夫听。 She read every line of the account aloud to her husband.
sceneCN: 这里 account 指账簿上逐笔记下的收支（第 2 个义项：账目）；句意为她把账目上的每一行念给丈夫听。

pos.zh: 名词：账户；账目；叙述；解释

derivatives.zh: 由本词加表示人的后缀 -ant 构成，义为「会计」
由本词加名词后缀 -ing 构成，义为「会计；会计工作」
由本词加后缀 -able 构成，义为「负有责任的；需要说明的」
由 accountable 加后缀 -ity 构成，义为「问责；责任」
由本词加后缀 -ancy 构成，义为「会计工作；会计行业」

senses.title: An arrangement with a bank
senses.definition: an arrangement in which a bank or similar organization keeps your money and records what you pay in and take out
senses.definitionCN: 由银行或类似机构替你保管钱财、记录存入与支出的一种安排
senses.example: I opened a savings account at the bank near my flat.
senses.exampleCN: 我在公寓附近的银行开了一个储蓄账户。
senses.why: The core image is a ledger line written under one name; a bank account is simply that line kept by an institution on your behalf.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是账簿上写着一个名字的一行；银行账户就是机构替你保管的那一行，所以「账户」直接从记账的动作里长出来。

senses.title: A record of money paid and owed
senses.definition: the record of money that has been received, spent, or is still owed, especially in business
senses.definitionCN: 收入、支出或尚未付清的钱款记录，尤用于商业往来
senses.example: The shopkeeper checked the account before closing up.
senses.exampleCN: 店主在打烊前核对了账目。
senses.why: The ledger itself is the core picture: setting down each sum in order is exactly what the older word for reckoning named.
senses.whyCN: 账簿本身就是核心画面：把每一笔钱按顺序记下来，正是这个表示「核算」的古词所指的动作。

senses.title: A spoken or written report
senses.definition: a description of an event or situation, given by someone who saw it or knows about it
senses.definitionCN: 由目睹或了解情况的人对事件、处境所作的描述
senses.example: By her account, the meeting ended before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 按她的说法，会议在中午前就结束了。
senses.why: To keep accounts is to set events down one by one; telling what happened is the same ordering act, so the ledger word also means a story told.
senses.whyCN: 记账是把事情一条条列清楚；讲述发生了什么也是同一种排序的动作，于是账簿的词也用来指讲出来的那一版说法。

senses.title: A reason or explanation
senses.definition: an explanation that makes something clear, especially one that answers for a fault or a difference
senses.definitionCN: 使某事变得清楚的说明，尤指为过失或差额作出的交代
senses.example: He could give no account of the missing money.
senses.exampleCN: 他说不清那笔钱去了哪里。
senses.why: An account has to balance; when the figures do not match, someone must supply the words that explain the gap, and those words become an account.
senses.whyCN: 账要能对得上；当数字对不上时，总得有人说出话来解释差额，这些话就成了「解释」。

senses.title: To form a share of a total
senses.definition: to be a particular part or proportion of a whole, especially of an amount or a total
senses.definitionCN: 构成整体中的某一部分或比例，尤指金额或总数中的一份
senses.example: Rent accounts for half of their monthly spending.
senses.exampleCN: 房租占他们每月开销的一半。
senses.why: Split a total into ledger lines and each line is a portion; saying how much one line takes up is the accounting verb turned into a statement of proportion.
senses.whyCN: 把总数拆成一行行账目，每一行都是一份；说清某一行占去多少，就是记账的动词变成了「占比」的说法。

senses.title: Credit; payment at a later date
senses.definition: an arrangement in which goods or services are supplied now and paid for later
senses.definitionCN: 先取得商品或服务、以后再付款的一种安排
senses.example: They bought the sofa on account and paid it off in May.
senses.exampleCN: 他们赊账买了那张沙发，五月才付清。
senses.why: A ledger can be written forward in time: take the goods now, put the debt on the line, settle it later. The record becomes a form of credit.
senses.whyCN: 账目可以往后记：现在拿走货物，把欠款记在这一行，以后再结清；记录本身就变成了一种赊欠。

senses.title: A client or business relationship
senses.definition: a customer, especially one that a company serves regularly and earns money from
senses.definitionCN: 客户，尤指公司长期服务并从中获利的对象
senses.example: The design firm lost its biggest account last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这家设计公司去年春天失去了最大的客户。
senses.why: One ledger line stands for one paying party; by transference the line comes to mean the person or company behind it.
senses.whyCN: 账簿上的一行代表一个付钱的一方；经由转喻，这一行就转而指它背后的那个人或公司。

senses.title: To regard someone as something
senses.definition: to judge or consider someone or something to be a certain thing, especially in a formal statement
senses.definitionCN: 判定或认为某人某物属于某种情况，尤用于正式表述
senses.example: The team was accounted a great success.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍被认为取得了巨大成功。
senses.why: Reckoning means putting each item into its proper column; to account a person brave or a plan sound is to file them under that heading.
senses.whyCN: 核算就是把每一项放进该放的栏目；把一个人记成勇敢、把一个方案记成稳妥，就是把它归入那一栏，于是有了「认为、视为」。

intro.en: Account comes from a French phrase meaning 'to a count', built on Latin computare 'to reckon'; the money sense and the story sense grew from the same act of counting.
intro.cn: account 来自古法语中表示「照着数一遍」的短语，源头是拉丁语 computare「核算」；钱的意义与叙述的意义都从同一个「数」的动作长出来。

items.en: Putare meant 'to reckon, consider, judge'. It is generally explained from an older sense 'to prune, trim', though how cutting came to mean judging is still discussed.
items.cn: putare 意为「估算、认为、判断」。一般认为它有更早的「修剪」义，但「修剪」如何过渡到「判断」仍有讨论。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus putare gave computare, 'to reckon together, calculate'; it is the direct source of both count and account.
items.cn: com-「一起」加 putare 构成 computare，意为「合起来核算、计算」，是 count 与 account 的直接源头。

items.en: The phrase a + conte, literally 'to a count', became acont 'a reckoning, an instalment'; the verb conter meant 'to count, to tell'.
items.cn: 短语 a + conte 字面是「照着数一遍」，合成 acont，意为「核算、分期付款」；动词 conter 意为「数、讲述」。

items.en: The noun is recorded from about 1300 for a reckoning of money; the verb 'to count, reckon' follows, and the sense 'explain' appears later.
items.cn: 名词约在 1300 年有记录，指钱财的核算；动词「数、核算」随后出现，「解释」义更晚才成形。

items.en: Banking gave the word its everyday 'bank account' sense, while trade gave 'on account' for credit and 'account' for a regular client.
items.cn: 银行业带来日常的「银行账户」义，商业往来则带来赊账的 on account，以及指长期客户的 account。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the derived family and the Latin relatives of to count; the near-meaning group gathers documents and reports that record money or events.
note.cn: 形近组收由本词派生的词族，以及同出「计算」一源的亲属词；近义组收记录钱财或事件的单据与报告。

entries.definition: To add up numbers or keep a tally; it comes from the same Latin verb computare.
