entries.definition: A printed record of money paid in and out, especially one sent by a bank.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「对账单、结算单」，尤指银行寄出的收支记录。

entries.definition: A factual spoken or written description of an event.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「报告、报道」，指对事件的事实性叙述。

entries.definition: A connected story or description of events.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「叙述、叙事」，指连贯讲述事件的版本。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real French phrase behind the word and the fixed phrases it appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用这个词背后真实的法语短语，以及它固定出现的搭配。

normal.en: The word is a plus count: a reckoning written down under a name.
normal.cn: 这个词就是 a 加 count：写在一个名字底下的一笔核算。

normal.en: Latin computare gives both count and account, so to account for something is to give the count that explains it.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 computare 同时给出 count 与 account，所以 account for 就是拿出能解释它的那笔核算。

normal.en: A bank account is a ledger line that an institution keeps for you.
normal.cn: 银行账户就是机构替你保管的一行账。

normal.en: On account means the goods are put on the ledger now and paid for later.
normal.cn: on account 意为货物先记在账上，钱以后再付。

normal.en: Take account of means to put something into your reckoning before you decide.
normal.cn: take account of 意为在下判断之前把某事物算进你的核算里。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger open on a counter, one line for each name.
abstract.cn: 想象一本摊在柜台上的账簿，每个名字占一行。

abstract.en: The same line can hold coins, a story or a reason, because all three are things set down in order.
abstract.cn: 同一行账可以装钱、装一段经历，也可以装一个理由，因为这三样都是被按顺序记下来的东西。

abstract.en: When the numbers do not add up, someone has to give an account of the gap.
abstract.cn: 当数字对不上时，总得有人为那点差额给出一个说法。

examples.en: I opened a savings account at the bank near my flat.
examples.cn: 我在公寓附近的银行开了一个储蓄账户。

examples.en: By her account, the meeting ended before noon.
examples.cn: 按她的说法，会议在中午前就结束了。

examples.en: Rent accounts for half of their monthly spending.
examples.cn: 房租占他们每月开销的一半。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿康特」——阿康把每一笔都记在账本上，还要讲清来龙去脉：账户、账目、叙述、解释。

root: 古法语 à + conte「照着数一遍」合成 acont，源头是拉丁语 computare「核算」，由 com-「一起」+ putare「估算、认为」构成。putare 更早的「修剪」义一般认为成立，但由「修剪」到「判断」的过渡仍有讨论。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses come from one act of setting things down in order: a ledger line for money, the same order applied to events, to an explanation, to a share, to credit, to a client, and finally to a judgement.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都来自同一个「按顺序记下」的动作：为钱记一行，再把同样的顺序用到事件、解释、份额、赊欠、客户，最后用到对人的判断上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open ledger on a counter, one line for each name, every coin set down in order.
core.cn: 核心意象：柜台上摊开的账簿，每个名字一行，每一枚钱币都按顺序记下。

branches.en: MONEY KEPT: the ledger line becomes an account held with a bank, or a record of what is owed.
branches.cn: 钱之线：账簿上的一行变成银行替你保管的账户，或一笔应收应付的记录。

branches.en: STORY TOLD: counting events one by one produces a reported version of what happened.
branches.cn: 叙述线：把事件一件件数出来，就得到关于所发生之事的说法。

branches.en: GAP EXPLAINED: when the figures do not match, the account becomes the reason offered for the difference.
branches.cn: 解释线：当数字对不上时，account 就变成为差额给出的理由。

branches.en: PORTION AND CREDIT: one line can be a share of the total, or goods written down to be paid later.
branches.cn: 份额与赊欠线：一行账可以是总额中的一份，也可以是先记下、以后再付的货物。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND JUDGEMENT: a line stands for a regular client, and to account someone is to file them under a heading.
branches.cn: 人与评判线：一行账可以代表长期客户，而把某人归到某一栏，就是对他作出判断。

intro.en: Account is a French phrase frozen into one word, with Latin pieces underneath; English adds familiar endings to build the family.
intro.cn: account 是一个凝固成单词的法语短语，底下是拉丁语的构件；英语再用常见词尾扩展出这一词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin putare and computare are both recorded, so only the oldest sense development of putare remains uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 putare 与 computare 均有文献记录，只有 putare 最早的语义演变尚有不确定之处。

items.example: It joins putare to make computare.
items.exampleCN: 它与 putare 结合构成 computare。

items.example: Putare is the reckoning root of the family.
items.exampleCN: putare 是这一词族表示「核算」的词根。

items.example: Computare gives both count and account.
items.exampleCN: computare 同时产生 count 与 account。

items.meaning: a count, a reckoning, a story
items.exampleCN: a 加 conte 合成了 acont。

items.example: Conter already joined counting and telling.
items.exampleCN: conter 已经把「数」与「讲述」合在一起。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb from com- and putare

derivatives.zh: 由本词加表示人的后缀 -ant 构成，义为「会计」
由本词加名词后缀 -ing 构成，义为「会计；会计工作」
由本词加后缀 -able 构成，义为「负有责任的；需要说明的」
由 accountable 加后缀 -ity 构成，义为「问责；责任」

definition_en: a person whose job is to examine places, goods, or work and report on them
core_image: 一个带着记录本的人站在楼梯口，正在逐项核对清单
scene: 工厂门口贴着来访须知，穿制服的人把证件挂在胸前。 The inspector wrote down three faults and asked to see them fixed by Friday.
sceneCN: 这里 inspector 是「检查员」（第 1 个义项：以检查场所、货物或工作为职业的人），句意是检查员记下了三处问题，并要求周五前修好。画面里能看到的物件：记录本、清单、证件。

pos.zh: 名词：检查员；督察；巡视员

derivatives.zh: 由本词换后缀构成，义为「检查；视察」
同族动词，义为「检查；视察」
由本词加 -ate 构成，义为「检查机构；督察部门」
由本词加 -ship 构成，义为「检查员职位」

senses.title: A person who examines officially
senses.definition: someone employed to look closely at buildings, food, machines, or work and report the results
senses.definitionCN: 受雇仔细查看建筑、食品、机器或工作并上报结果的人
senses.example: A health inspector closed the kitchen for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 卫生检查员把厨房关停了一周。
senses.why: The agent ending -or turns the act of looking into the person who does it.
senses.whyCN: 施事后缀 -or 把「看」这个动作变成做这个动作的人。

senses.title: A police rank
senses.definition: a police officer of middle rank, above a sergeant in many forces
senses.definitionCN: 许多警队中位于警长之上、属中层警衔的警官
senses.example: Inspector Brown took charge of the case.
senses.exampleCN: 布朗警督负责此案。
senses.why: Looking into crimes became an office with a name; the one who investigates is the inspector.
senses.whyCN: 「查察案件」变成了一种职务，负责查案的人就称为 inspector。

senses.title: A supervisor of schools or services
senses.definition: an official who visits schools or public services to check their standards
senses.definitionCN: 到访学校或公共服务机构检查其水平的官员
senses.example: The inspector sat at the back and said nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 督学坐在后排，一言不发。
senses.why: The word spread from factories to schools and railways, wherever standards had to be watched.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从工厂传到学校与铁路，凡是需要监督标准的地方都有它。

intro.en: Inspector is the Latin agent noun from inspicere "to look into", meaning literally "the one who looks in".
intro.cn: inspector 是拉丁语 inspicere「向里看」的施事名词，字面就是「往里看的人」。

items.en: Specere "to look" and the compound inspicere "to examine" are both classical.
items.cn: specere「看」与复合词 inspicere「查察」都是古典拉丁语词汇。

items.en: The agent suffix -or marked the person performing the action.
items.cn: 施事后缀 -or 标出执行动作的人。

items.en: Late Latin used inspector for an overseer or examiner.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语用 inspector 指监工或查察者。

items.en: Old French inspecteur passed the word to English in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 inspecteur 在十七世纪把这个词传给英语。

items.en: Railways, factories and police forces each created their own inspectors.
items.cn: 铁路、工厂与警队各自设立了自己的 inspector 职位。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the spec- root and the -or agent pattern; the near-meaning group holds other watching jobs.
note.cn: 形近组共享 spec- 词根与 -or 施事模式；近义组收其他「查看类」职业名词。

entries.definition: The verb that names the action the inspector performs.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，即 inspector 所执行的动作。

entries.definition: The act or occasion of looking into something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「检查、视察」。

entries.definition: A watcher with no duty to report anything.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「观众」，只观看而无报告之责。

entries.definition: Someone who checks accounts rather than buildings.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「审计员」，查的是账目而不是建筑。

entries.definition: Someone who watches over staff day by day.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「主管」，日常监管员工。

entries.definition: A specialist who measures and inspects buildings or land.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「测量员、鉴定人」，专查建筑或土地。

normalIntro.en: These hooks connect the -or ending with the job and recall the real official titles.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把 -or 词尾与职业联系起来，并复习真实的官衔。

normal.en: Inspect plus -or: the one who looks in.
normal.cn: inspect 加 -or：往里看的那个人。

normal.en: An inspector writes down what others walked past.
normal.cn: 检查员记下别人走过时忽略的东西。

normal.en: Health, fire and school all have inspectors.
normal.cn: 卫生、消防、学校都设有检查员。

normal.en: Inspector is also a police rank in Britain.
normal.cn: inspector 在英国也是警衔。

normal.en: The inspectorate is the whole office of inspectors.
normal.cn: inspectorate 指检查员组成的整个机构。

abstract.en: Picture a clipboard with legs walking the corridor.
abstract.cn: 想象一块带腿的板夹走在走廊里。

abstract.en: The inspector stands where the rules meet the real world.
abstract.cn: 检查员站在规则与现实的交界处。

abstract.en: To be inspected is to be seen as you really are.
abstract.cn: 被检查就是被如实看见。

examples.en: The inspector found broken tiles on the roof.
examples.cn: 检查员发现屋顶有破损的瓦片。

examples.en: An inspector will visit the kitchen next week.
examples.cn: 检查员下周会来厨房查看。

examples.en: She was promoted to inspector after ten years.
examples.cn: 十年后她晋升为警督。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因斯派克特」——专门派来查看的人，就是检查员

root: 拉丁语 specere「看」→ inspicere「查察」→ 施事后缀 -or 构成晚期拉丁语 inspector「监工、查察者」→ 古法语 inspecteur → 十七世纪英语 inspector。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the official examiner, the police rank, and the school or service supervisor.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：官方检查员、警督，以及督学类督导。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person with a notebook stands at the foot of the stairs, ticking off a list.
core.cn: 核心意象：拿着记录本的人站在楼梯口，逐项打勾。

branches.en: THE FACTORY: the examiner of goods, food and machines.
branches.cn: 工厂这条线：检查货物、食品与机器的人。

branches.en: THE STATION: a police rank built on investigation.
branches.cn: 警局这条线：由「查案」发展出的警衔。

branches.en: THE CLASSROOM: the visiting supervisor of schools.
branches.cn: 教室这条线：到访学校的督学。

branches.en: THE LINK: all three share the duty of looking and reporting.
branches.cn: 连接线：三者都负有查看并上报之责。

branches.en: THE TONE: as a job title the word is neutral and official.
branches.cn: 语气线：作为职务名称，这个词中性而正式。

intro.en: Inspector is the stem inspect- plus the Latin agent ending -or "one who".
intro.cn: inspector 是词干 inspect- 加拉丁施事词尾 -or「做……的人」。

latinIntro.en: Latin inspicere and inspector are recorded; the agent suffix -or is regular.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 inspicere 与 inspector 均有记载，施事后缀 -or 是规则词尾。

items.example: The prefix marks the inward look.
It turns the action into a person.
The noun names what the inspector does.
items.exampleCN: 名词指 inspector 所做的事。

items.example: The suffix -ate marks a collective body.
A near-by job title from the same idea.
Another checker with a narrower field.
items.exampleCN: 另一位检查者，范围更窄。
检查的是建筑而非产品。

definition_en: something useful that can be used to achieve a goal
core_image: 仓库里整齐码放着工具、材料和食物，随时可以取用
scene: 岛上淡水有限，居民很早就学会珍惜每一份资源。 Fresh water is limited on the island, so residents learned early to value every resource.
sceneCN: 这里 resource 是「资源」（第 1 个义项：可利用的有用之物）；句意：岛上淡水有限，居民很早就学会珍惜每一份资源。

senses.title: A useful supply
senses.definition: a supply of something such as water, fuel, or money that can be used
senses.definitionCN: 水、燃料或资金等可供使用的供应
senses.example: The country is rich in natural resources.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家自然资源丰富。
senses.why: The word names a source to which one can return for help.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指可以反复回来求助的来源。

senses.title: Personal ability to cope
senses.definition: the ability to find a way through a difficult situation
senses.definitionCN: 在困难处境中找到出路的能力
senses.example: She showed great resource in a crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 她在危机中表现出很强的应变能力。
senses.why: A person's inner reserves are a resource drawn on in trouble.
senses.whyCN: 一个人的内在储备，就是困难时可取用的资源。

senses.title: A teaching or reference material
senses.definition: a book, website, or other material used for learning or reference
senses.definitionCN: 用于学习或查阅的书、网站或其他材料
senses.example: The website is a useful resource for teachers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个网站对教师来说是很有用的资源。
senses.why: Any material one can draw on for a task is a resource.
senses.whyCN: 任何可供任务取用的材料都是资源。

intro.en: Resource comes from French ressource, a source of help, from Old French resourdre, to rise again, ultimately Latin resurgere.
intro.cn: resource 来自法语 ressource（求助之源），源于古法语 resourdre（重新升起），最终来自拉丁语 resurgere。

items.en: Surgere means to rise.
items.cn: surgere 意为升起。

items.en: Resurgere means to rise again.
items.cn: resurgere 意为重新升起。

items.en: Resourdre means to rise again or recover.
items.cn: resourdre 意为再起、恢复。

items.en: Ressource means a source of help or recovery.
items.cn: ressource 意为求助或恢复的来源。

items.en: English resource covers means of support and available supplies.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪，英语 resource 涵盖支持手段与可用物资。

items.en: Modern English often uses the plural for a country's wealth.
items.cn: 现代英语常用复数指一个国家的财富。

note.en: Resource is a source one draws on, and it sits near its family and near words for supplies and means.
note.cn: resource 是一个可取用的来源，与自身词族以及表示供应和手段的词相邻。

entries.definition: good at finding ways to solve problems
entries.definitionCN: 足智多谋的

entries.definition: in a clever and practical way
entries.definitionCN: 足智多谋地

entries.definition: the ability to cope cleverly
entries.definitionCN: 应变能力

entries.definition: an amount of something available
entries.definitionCN: 供应；储备

entries.definition: something valuable that can be used
entries.definitionCN: 资产；有用之物

entries.definition: a method or resource for doing something
entries.definitionCN: 手段；财力

normalIntro.en: Resource is a source one can rise back to: something useful kept ready.
normalIntro.cn: resource 是一个可以回头依靠的来源：随时备好的有用之物。

normal.en: The re- suggests rising again when needed.
normal.cn: re- 暗示需要时能再站起来。

normal.en: Natural resources are supplies taken from the earth.
normal.cn: 自然资源取自大地。

normal.en: Human resources are the people an organisation can draw on.
normal.cn: 人力资源是组织可以依靠的人。

normal.en: A resourceful person finds a way with very little.
normal.cn: resourceful 的人用很少的东西也能找到办法。

normal.en: Compare source: a source supplies, while a resource is a source you can use.
normal.cn: 对比 source：source 提供来源，resource 是可供你使用的来源。

abstract.en: Picture shelves of tools and food neatly stacked.
abstract.cn: 想象架子上整齐放着工具和食物。

abstract.en: Imagine a small boat with one oar used cleverly.
abstract.cn: 想象一条小船，靠一支桨巧妙前行。

abstract.en: Think of a teacher's box of ready-made materials.
abstract.cn: 想象老师一盒备好的教学材料。

examples.en: The country is rich in natural resources.
examples.cn: 这个国家自然资源丰富。

examples.en: She showed great resource in a crisis.
examples.cn: 她在危机中表现出很强的应变能力。

examples.en: The website is a useful resource for teachers.
examples.cn: 这个网站对教师来说是很有用的资源。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re + source」——可以反复回去取用的来源，就是资源；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 surgere（升起）→ resurgere（再起）→ 古法语 resourdre → ressource（求助之源）→ 现代英语 resource。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts with a source of help one can return to, then covers material supplies, inner coping ability, and learning materials.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从可以回去求助的来源开始，再涵盖物资储备、内在应变能力与学习材料。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a store of useful things ready to be drawn on.
core.cn: 核心意象：一批随时可取用的有用之物。

branches.en: Material supply is the basic modern sense.
branches.cn: 物资供应，是基本现代义项。

branches.en: Inner ability is a resource stored in a person.
branches.cn: 内在能力，是储存在人身上的资源。

branches.en: Learning material is a resource drawn on for a task.
branches.cn: 学习材料是为任务取用的资源。

branches.en: Countries and people both draw on reserves in hard times.
branches.cn: 国家与人都会在困难时动用储备。

branches.en: A clever person and a good website both help solve problems.
branches.cn: 聪明的人与好网站都能帮助解决问题。

intro.en: Resource is a French-shaped noun built on the Latin verb for rising again, with English endings forming its family.
intro.cn: resource 是建立在拉丁语「再起」动词上的法语形态名词，词族由英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin surgere means to rise, and resurgere means to rise again.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 surgere 意为升起，resurgere 意为重新升起。

items.example: Re- adds the sense of rising again.
Resurgere joins the prefix and the root.
items.exampleCN: resurgere 把前缀与词根结合。

items.example: Resourdre carries the verb into French.
items.exampleCN: resourdre 把这个动词带入法语。

items.example: Ressource is the direct source of resource.
items.exampleCN: ressource 是 resource 的直接来源。
resource 保留「求助之源」的含义。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的词尾

definition_en: a main division of a book, a distinct period in a history or life, or a local branch of an organization
core_image: 一本书被书签分开的一段
scene: 夜深了，书页翻到新的部分。 She stopped reading at the third chapter.
sceneCN: 这里 chapter 指「章」（第 1 个义项：书中的主要分节）；句意是她在第三章停下阅读。

senses.title: A main division of a book
senses.definition: one of the main parts into which a book or long text is divided
senses.definitionCN: 书或长文被分成的主要部分之一
senses.example: The first chapter sets the scene.
senses.exampleCN: 第一章交代了背景。
senses.why: Latin capitulum meant a little head, the heading written at the start of each section.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 capitulum 意为小头，即写在每节开头的小标题。

senses.title: A period in a life or history
senses.definition: a distinct period in someone's life or in the history of something
senses.definitionCN: 某人一生或某事历史中界限分明的一段
senses.example: That chapter of her life is closed.
senses.exampleCN: 她人生的那一章已经翻过去了。
senses.why: A section of a story was borrowed for a stretch of time that reads like a story.
senses.whyCN: 故事的一节被借来形容一段读起来像故事的时间。

senses.title: A local branch of a society
senses.definition: a local branch of a club, society or religious body
senses.definitionCN: 俱乐部、协会或宗教团体的地方分支
senses.example: The local chapter meets on Fridays.
senses.exampleCN: 地方分会每周五聚会。
senses.why: Members gathered under one heading formed a chapter, and the word passed to the group itself.
senses.whyCN: 在同一标题下聚集的成员构成一个 chapter，这个词又转指这群人本身。

intro.en: Chapter descends from Latin caput, a head, through the little heading written at the start of a section.
intro.cn: chapter 源自拉丁语 caput（头），经由写在一节开头的小标题而来。

items.en: Caput meant the head.
items.cn: 拉丁语 caput 意为头。

items.en: Capitulum was a little head, used for a heading.
items.cn: capitulum 意为小头，用来指标题。

items.en: Chapitre named a division of a book and a body of clergy.
items.cn: chapitre 指书中的分节，也指一群教士。

items.en: English chapter named both a book section and a cathedral body.
items.cn: 英语 chapter 同时指书中分节与主教座堂的教士团。

items.en: The word now also means a period of time and a local branch.
items.cn: 如今该词还指一段时期与地方分会。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cap- head root, while the meaning group lists parts and phases.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cap-「头」词根，近义组列出部分与阶段。

entries.definition: the chief city or money for investment
entries.definitionCN: 首都或投资本金

entries.definition: the leader of a team or ship
entries.definitionCN: 队伍或船只的领导者

entries.definition: more than one chapter
entries.definitionCN: 章的复数形式

entries.definition: one part of a whole text
entries.definitionCN: 整体文本的一部分

entries.definition: one event in a longer series
entries.definitionCN: 较长系列中的一个事件

entries.definition: a local office of an organization
entries.definitionCN: 组织的地方机构

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the head root, the phrase a new chapter and the local branch sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「头」词根、短语 a new chapter 以及地方分会义。

normal.en: Chapter and capital share caput, the Latin head, because a chapter begins with a heading.
normal.cn: chapter 与 capital 共享拉丁语 caput（头），因为一章从一个标题开始。

normal.en: A new chapter is a fresh period, not a new book.
normal.cn: a new chapter 指新的阶段，而不是一本新书。

normal.en: Chapter and verse means you can cite the exact place.
normal.cn: chapter and verse 意为能引出确切出处。

normal.en: A local chapter is a branch that meets under one name.
normal.cn: local chapter 是在同一名下聚会的地方分支。

normal.en: The plural chapters adds an s and appears in chapter titles.
normal.cn: 复数 chapters 加 s，常出现在章节标题里。

abstract.en: Picture a bookmark closing one part of a story.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚书签合上故事的一段。

abstract.en: Picture a turned page with a large number at the top.
abstract.cn: 想象翻过的一页，顶端印着大大的数字。

abstract.en: Picture a small group of members raising hands in a side room.
abstract.cn: 想象一小群成员在小房间里举手。

examples.en: The book has twelve chapters.
examples.cn: 这本书有十二章。

examples.en: Moving abroad opened a new chapter in his life.
examples.cn: 移居国外为他的人生打开了新篇章。

examples.en: The student chapter organized a charity run.
examples.cn: 学生分会组织了一场慈善长跑。

dict_mnemonic.text: chapter 与 capital 同源，都来自「头」（caput）：一章就是一段文字的「头」。

root: 源自拉丁语 caput（头）的指小形式 capitulum（小头、标题），经古法语 chapitre 进入英语；与 capital、captain 同根。

sensesIntro.en: A heading marks off a book section, and that section became a period of time and a branch of members.
sensesIntro.cn: 标题划出书中的一节，这一节又变成一段时期与一群成员的分支。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heading that opens a new section.
core.cn: 核心意象：开启新一节的那个标题。

branches.en: A chapter heading divides a long text.
branches.cn: 章节标题把长文分开。

branches.en: A closed chapter marks the end of a period.
branches.cn: 翻过去的一章标志一段时期的结束。

branches.en: A local chapter gathers members under one heading.
branches.cn: 地方分会在同一标题下聚集成员。

branches.en: Both senses borrow the shape of a story.
branches.cn: 两个义项都借用了故事的形态。

branches.en: Text divisions and member groups share the heading.
branches.cn: 文本分节与成员团体共享「标题」。

intro.en: Chapter keeps the cap- head root found in capital and captain.
intro.cn: chapter 保留在 capital 与 captain 中可见的 cap-「头」词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin caput and its diminutive capitulum are the head and the heading behind the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 caput 及其指小形式 capitulum 是这个词背后的「头」与「标题」。

items.meaning: a meeting house of a branch

items.example: The capital lies to the north.

definition_zh: 平台；站台；讲台；政纲；立足点
definition_en: a raised flat surface for people to stand on, a station area beside tracks, or a set of political promises
core_image: 一片被抬高、垫平的板面——人站上去，声音和列车都从这里出发
scene: 候车的人们站在黄线后面，眼睛盯着显示屏上的车次。 The passengers waited on the platform for the morning express.
sceneCN: 这里是「站台」（第 2 个义项：铁路轨道旁供上下车的平台）；句意为乘客们在站台上等早班快车。画面就是那片抬起的人造平地。

derivatives.zh: platform 加 -er 构成的名词，义为「平台跳跃类游戏」
cross 与 platform 合成，义为「跨平台的」

senses.title: A raised flat surface
senses.definition: a raised level surface built for people or things to stand on
senses.definitionCN: 为让人或物立足而建的抬高平面
senses.example: The speaker stepped onto the wooden platform.
senses.exampleCN: 发言人走上木讲台。
senses.why: French plate-forme joined flatness to shape: literally a flat form lifted above the ground.
senses.whyCN: 法语 plate-forme 把「平」与「形」结合：字面即抬离地面的平坦形体。

senses.title: A station area beside tracks
senses.definition: the raised area beside railway tracks where passengers board
senses.definitionCN: 铁轨旁供乘客上下车的抬高地面
senses.example: Mind the gap between the train and the platform.
senses.exampleCN: 小心列车与站台之间的空隙。
senses.why: The raised surface became the place where journeys start and end.
senses.whyCN: 抬高的平面变成了旅程开始与结束之处。

senses.title: A set of political promises
senses.definition: the declared aims and promises of a political party
senses.definitionCN: 政党宣布的目标与承诺
senses.example: Tax reform stands first in their platform.
senses.exampleCN: 税改列在他们政纲的第一条。
senses.why: The party stands on its promises as on a raised stage, presenting itself to be seen.
senses.whyCN: 政党站在承诺之上如同站在高台，把自己呈现给众人看。

senses.title: A base technology for others to build on
senses.definition: a system on which software or services are built and run
senses.definitionCN: 承载软件或服务构建与运行的系统
senses.example: The app runs on every major platform.
senses.exampleCN: 这个应用在所有主流平台上都能运行。
senses.why: Technology borrowed the raised surface: a base others stand on to build higher.
senses.whyCN: 技术界借走这个抬高的平面：让别人站上去建更高的楼。

senses.title: A position from which to speak or act
senses.definition: a chance or position from which one can express views or act
senses.definitionCN: 可以表达观点或采取行动的机会或位置
senses.example: The award gave her a platform to defend the wetlands.
senses.exampleCN: 这个奖项给了她一个为湿地发声的讲坛。
senses.why: Standing on a platform makes a person taller and more visible, so the word moved to influence itself.
senses.whyCN: 站上高台让人更高、更显眼，这个词便移向影响力本身。

intro.en: Platform is French plate-forme in disguise: a flat (plate) form raised above the ground for standing on.
intro.cn: platform 是法语 plate-forme 的变装：一个抬离地面供人立足的平坦（plate）形体。

items.en: Plate-forme combined plate, flat, with forme, shape.
items.cn: 法语 plate-forme 由 plate（平的）与 forme（形）合成。

items.en: Plate descends from Latin plattus or Greek platys, broad and flat.
items.cn: plate 可追至拉丁语 plattus 或希腊语 platys（宽、平）。

items.en: English borrowed platform in the sixteenth century for raised structures.
items.cn: 英语十六世纪借入 platform，指抬高的构筑物。

items.en: The coming of railways fixed the station-platform sense in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 十九世纪铁路兴起，确立了站台义。

items.en: Politics, computing and media each stand on the word today.
items.cn: 如今政治、计算与媒体各踩着这个词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the flat-family; the near-meaning group gathers raised bases and stages.
note.cn: 形近组收「平」词族；近义组收抬高基座与舞台词。

entries.definition: Flat highland or a stalled stage of progress; shares the plate- root.
entries.definitionCN: 平坦高地或停滞阶段；同 plate- 词根。

entries.definition: A flat dish or metal sheet; the closest English cousin.
entries.definitionCN: 扁平餐具或金属板；最近的英语表亲。

entries.definition: A precious metal; begins with plat- but its name comes from Spanish plata, silver.
entries.definitionCN: 贵金属；以 plat- 开头，但名称来自西班牙语 plata（银）。

entries.definition: A raised floor for performers, also a phase of progress.
entries.definitionCN: 供演出者使用的抬高地板，也指进程阶段。

entries.definition: A small raised stand for a speaker or conductor.
entries.definitionCN: 演讲者或指挥用的小高台。

entries.definition: The foundation something stands on, physical or abstract.
entries.definitionCN: 某物立足的基础，物理或抽象。

normalIntro.en: One image — a raised flat floor — carries stations, stages, manifestos and software alike.
normalIntro.cn: 一个意象——抬高的平面地板——同时承载站台、讲台、政纲与软件。

normal.en: Platform is literally a flat form: plate + form.
normal.cn: platform 字面就是「平的形」：plate 加 form。

normal.en: Mind the gap is said only on platforms.
normal.cn: mind the gap 只在站台里说。

normal.en: A political platform is the stage a party stands on.
normal.cn: 政治政纲就是政党站立的舞台。

normal.en: Every app needs a platform to stand on.
normal.cn: 每个应用都需要可以立足的平台。

normal.en: A platform makes the small speaker taller than the crowd.
normal.cn: 讲台让矮小的发言者高过人群。

abstract.en: A raised deck of boards above the mud, everyone stepping up onto it.
abstract.cn: 泥地上方一块木板高台，人们逐级踩上去。

abstract.en: A train sliding in, its windows level with waiting feet.
abstract.cn: 一列火车滑进站，车窗与候车人的脚齐平。

abstract.en: A microphone lifted above an audience, voices radiating outward.
abstract.cn: 一支话筒被举到观众上方，声音向外扩散。

examples.en: The train drew slowly into platform three.
examples.cn: 列车缓缓驶入三号站台。

examples.en: The party's platform promised lower taxes.
examples.cn: 该党政纲承诺减税。

examples.en: She used her fame as a platform for climate action.
examples.cn: 她把名声用作推动气候行动的平台。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普莱特福姆」——铺平了、抬高了的台，站上去万事从这出发；platform 就是平台。

root: platform 源自法语 plate-forme（平坦的形体），plate 可追至拉丁语 plattus 或希腊语 platys（宽、平），forme 出自拉丁语 forma（形）；由「抬高的平面」引申出站台、讲台、政纲与技术平台。

sensesIntro.en: A flat form raised above the mud becomes a station edge, a speaker's stage, a party's promises and a software base.
sensesIntro.cn: 一块抬离泥地的平坦形体，变成车站的边缘、发言者的讲台、政党的承诺和软件的基座。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat surface lifted so that everyone can see and step onto it.
core.cn: 核心意象：被抬起的平面，让人人可见、可踏足。

branches.en: the deck lifted above the mud
branches.cn: 抬离泥地的木板台

branches.en: the yellow line by the rails
branches.cn: 铁轨旁的黄线

branches.en: the promises raised for all to read
branches.cn: 被举起来供众人读的承诺

branches.en: the voice lifted above the crowd
branches.cn: 被举过人群的嗓音

branches.en: from wooden decks to digital bases
branches.cn: 从木板台到数字基座

intro.en: Platform is a compound of two borrowed roots, flat and shape, which keeps expanding into modern compounds.
intro.cn: platform 是「平」与「形」两个借入词根的复合词，如今不断长出新的复合词。

latinIntro.en: The plate- flatness root also lives in plate, plateau and platter.
latinIntro.cn: plate- 的「平」词根也活在 plate、plateau 与 platter 里。

latinEntries.meaning: an English derivative of the headword
latinEntries.meaningCN: platform 加 -er 构成，义为「平台跳跃游戏」

latinEntries.meaning: an English derivative of the headword
latinEntries.meaningCN: cross 与 platform 合成，义为「跨平台的」

definition_en: the quality of being beautiful, or a beautiful woman
core_image: 清晨花瓣上还未散去的露珠
scene: 露水在花瓣边缘聚成一颗。 The beauty of the garden surprised every visitor.
sceneCN: 这里 beauty 是「美」（第 1 个义项：使人愉悦的品质）；句意是花园之美让每位访客惊叹。

derivatives.zh: 由 beauty 加 -ful 构成，义为「美丽的」
由 beauty 加 -fy 构成，义为「美化」
由 beauty 与 -ician 构成，义为「美容师」

senses.title: The quality of being beautiful
senses.definition: the quality that gives pleasure to the senses
senses.definitionCN: 使感官愉悦的品质
senses.example: The beauty of the garden surprised every visitor.
senses.exampleCN: 花园之美让每位访客惊叹。
senses.why: The word came through French from Latin bellus, pretty.
senses.whyCN: 这个词经法语来自拉丁语 bellus「漂亮」。

senses.title: A beautiful woman or thing
senses.definition: a beautiful woman or a very fine example
senses.definitionCN: 美丽的女子或极出色的实例
senses.example: The old car is a real beauty.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆旧车真是件美物。
senses.why: The abstract quality was applied to the person or thing that shows it.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的品质被用来指体现它的美人或美物。

senses.title: The special advantage
senses.definition: the pleasing or useful feature of something
senses.definitionCN: 某事物令人愉快或有用的特点
senses.example: The beauty of it is that it costs nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 它的妙处在于不花一分钱。
senses.why: The sense of charm widened to any attractive advantage.
senses.whyCN: 「魅力」义扩展到任何吸引人的优点。

intro.en: Beauty came through French from a Latin word for pretty.
intro.cn: beauty 经法语来自拉丁语中表示「漂亮」的词。

items.en: bellus meant pretty or fine.
items.cn: bellus 意为「漂亮、美好」。

items.en: bel meant handsome or fair.
items.cn: bel 意为「俊美、美好」。

items.en: beaute named the quality of beauty.
items.cn: beaute 指「美」这一品质。

items.en: beaute entered English as beauty.
items.cn: beaute 进入英语，写作 beauty。

items.en: beauty covers looks, people and advantages.
items.cn: 如今 beauty 兼指外貌、美人与优点。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the same stem; the near-meaning group gives other words for charm.
note.cn: 形近组共享同一词干；近义组是其他表示魅力的词。

entries.definition: very pleasing to look at
entries.definitionCN: 美丽的

entries.definition: to make beautiful
entries.definitionCN: 美化

entries.definition: something you must do
entries.definitionCN: 责任

entries.definition: the power to please
entries.definitionCN: 魅力

entries.definition: graceful style
entries.definitionCN: 优雅

entries.definition: smooth beauty of movement
entries.definitionCN: 优美

normalIntro.en: Beauty is the quality behind beautiful.
normalIntro.cn: beauty 是 beautiful 背后的那种品质。

normal.en: The plural is beauties.
normal.cn: 复数是 beauties。

normal.en: Beautiful is beauty plus -ful.
normal.cn: beautiful 是 beauty 加 -ful。

normal.en: Beautify means to make beautiful.
normal.cn: beautify 指美化。

normal.en: A beauty salon is a place for personal care.
normal.cn: beauty salon 指美容院。

normal.en: The beauty of it means its special advantage.
normal.cn: the beauty of it 指它的妙处。

abstract.en: See dew resting on a petal.
abstract.cn: 想象停在花瓣上的露珠。

abstract.en: See a face that makes people turn.
abstract.cn: 想象一张让人回头的脸。

abstract.en: See a simple plan with one clear advantage.
abstract.cn: 想象一个有一个明显优点的简单方案。

examples.en: The beauty of the garden surprised every visitor.
examples.cn: 花园之美让每位访客惊叹。

examples.en: The old car is a real beauty.
examples.cn: 这辆旧车真是件美物。

examples.en: The beauty of it is that it costs nothing.
examples.cn: 它的妙处在于不花一分钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 beauty 想成清晨花瓣上那颗还没散去的露珠。

root: 源自拉丁语 bellus「漂亮」，经古法语 beaute 进入英语；由抽象的「美」引申指美人、美物，再引申为事物的「妙处」。

sensesIntro.en: The quality of beauty, the person who has it, and the advantage it brings.
sensesIntro.cn: 美的品质、拥有美的人，以及它带来的好处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: dew still resting on a petal.
core.cn: 核心意象：花瓣上未散的露珠。

branches.en: natural beauty
branches.cn: 自然之美

branches.en: the beauty of the garden
branches.cn: 花园之美

branches.en: a real beauty
branches.cn: 真正的美物

branches.en: the beauty of it
branches.cn: 它的妙处

branches.en: the beauty of the plan
branches.cn: 方案的妙处

intro.en: Beauty takes -ful, -fy and -ician to build new words.
intro.cn: beauty 可加 -ful、-fy、-ician 构成新词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is bellus, pretty.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基是 bellus，意为「漂亮」。

items.meaning: a person who cares for beauty

definition_en: a clear difference between things, or to compare them in order to show that difference
core_image: 黑白两块并排放着，边界格外清楚
scene: 展厅里两间屋子刷成一深一浅，站在门口就能看出差别。 The contrast between the two rooms is striking.
sceneCN: 这里 contrast 指「对比」（第 1 个义项：并置后显现的差异）；句意是两间屋子的对比非常鲜明。

collocations.phrase: the contrast between A and B
collocations.zh: A 与 B 之间的对比

senses.title: Side-by-side difference
senses.definition: a difference made clear by placing two things together
senses.definitionCN: 把两样东西并置之后显现出来的差异
senses.example: The contrast between the twins is obvious.
senses.exampleCN: 这对双胞胎的差异很明显。
senses.why: Two colours show their edge only next to each other.
senses.whyCN: 两种颜色只有并排时才显出边界。

senses.title: To set against
senses.definition: to compare two things in order to show how they differ
senses.definitionCN: 把两者放在一起比较以显出不同
senses.example: The report contrasts city life with country life.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把城市生活与乡村生活作对照。
senses.why: One picture explains another by standing beside it.
senses.whyCN: 一幅画靠着另一幅，就解释了它。

senses.title: A strong visual difference
senses.definition: the degree of difference between light and dark areas
senses.definitionCN: 明暗区域之间的差异程度
senses.example: Turn up the contrast on the screen.
senses.exampleCN: 把屏幕的反差调高一些。
senses.why: The eye reads edges before it reads shapes.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛先读边缘，再读形状。

intro.en: Contrast comes through French and Italian from Latin contra, against, and stare, to stand, so it first meant standing against.
intro.cn: contrast 经由法语和意大利语，来自拉丁语 contra（反对）与 stare（站立），本义是相对而立。

items.en: Stare meant to stand or stay in place.
items.cn: stare 意为站立或停在原处。

items.en: Contra stare meant to stand over against something.
items.cn: contra stare 意为站在某物的对面。

items.en: Contrasto named a quarrel and a facing of two sides.
items.cn: 意大利语 contrasto 指争执与两方对峙。

items.en: French contraste came to mean a striking difference.
items.cn: 法语 contraste 转指鲜明的差异。

items.en: English contrast was used for art and for argument.
items.cn: 英语 contrast 被用于绘画与论辩。

items.en: The word also names a dial on screens and cameras.
items.cn: 这个词也指屏幕和相机上的调节旋钮。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin standing base st-, and the meaning group names other words for difference and comparison.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的站立词基 st-，近义组列出其他表示差异与比较的词。

entries.definition: completely opposite to something
entries.definitionCN: 相反的

entries.definition: a formal written agreement
entries.definitionCN: 合同；契约

entries.definition: showing a difference between two things
entries.definitionCN: 表示对比的

entries.definition: the way in which things are not the same
entries.definitionCN: 差异；不同

entries.definition: the act of looking at two things together
entries.definitionCN: 比较；对照

entries.definition: the state of being against something
entries.definitionCN: 对立；反对

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with two things placed near each other, then move to comparing them and to the sharp edge of light and dark.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从被放在一起的两样东西开始，再到把它们作比较，最后到明暗之间那道利落的边。

normal.en: Contra- is against and st is stand, so contrast is two things standing face to face.
normal.cn: contra- 是相对，st 是站立，contrast 就是两样东西面对面站着。

normal.en: Put black beside white and both look stronger.
normal.cn: 把黑放在白旁边，两者都更有力。

normal.en: The noun is the gap, the verb is the act of showing it.
normal.cn: 名词是那道差距，动词是把它显出来的动作。

normal.en: A screen with more contrast hides the grey between.
normal.cn: 反差调高的屏幕，会藏起中间的灰。

normal.en: No second colour, no contrast.
normal.cn: 没有第二种颜色，就没有对比。

abstract.en: Picture two squares touching along one clean edge.
abstract.cn: 想象两个方块沿一条干净的边相接。

abstract.en: Picture a bright window in a dark wall.
abstract.cn: 想象深色墙上开着一扇明亮的窗。

abstract.en: Picture one hand open and one hand closed.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手张开，一只手握紧。

examples.en: The contrast between the two designs is clear.
examples.cn: 两个设计之间的对比很清楚。

examples.en: In contrast to last year, sales have risen.
examples.cn: 与去年相比，销售额上升了。

examples.en: The essay contrasts two ways of teaching.
examples.cn: 这篇文章对比了两种教学方式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 contrast 记成 contra（相对）加 st（站立）：两样东西面对面站着，差别一眼就看出来，就是对比。

root: 源自拉丁语 contra（反对）与 stare（站立），经由法语和意大利语进入英语，本义是相对而立，后指对比与反差。

sensesIntro.en: From two things placed near each other, to the act of comparing them, and at last to the edge between light and dark.
sensesIntro.cn: 从并排放着的两样东西，到把它们比较的动作，最后到明暗之间的那道边。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a black square laid against a white one.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块黑方块紧贴着一块白方块。

branches.en: Nearness makes the difference visible.
branches.cn: 靠近让差异变得可见。

branches.en: The verb does the work of putting them side by side.
branches.cn: 动词负责把它们并排放好。

branches.en: Light and dark give the word a technical life.
branches.cn: 明与暗让这个词有了技术上的用法。

branches.en: A difference and the act of showing it belong together.
branches.cn: 差异和把差异显出来的动作分不开。

branches.en: Comparing and tuning both sharpen an edge.
branches.cn: 作比较与作调节，都是在磨利一条边。

intro.en: Contrast is built on Latin contra, against, plus stare, to stand.
intro.cn: contrast 由拉丁语 contra（相对）与 stare（站立）构成。

latinIntro.en: The standing base st- also appears in stable, statue and constant.
latinIntro.cn: 站立词基 st- 也出现在 stable、statue 与 constant 中。

items.meaning: to stand two things face to face
items.meaningCN: 让两样东西面对面站着

items.meaning: making a difference easy to see
items.exampleCN: 他们穿了对比鲜明的颜色。

items.meaning: to draw into a smaller space
to set two things beside each other
the act of setting things together
items.meaningCN: 把事物并置比较的行为

definition_en: mainly, above all other things or purposes
core_image: 一栋房子的正门，旁边还有几扇小侧门
scene: 这座城市的经济靠港口，其他行业规模都小得多。 The city's economy is primarily dependent on the port.
sceneCN: 这里指首要、占主导（第 1 个义项：主要地）；句意为这座城市的经济主要依赖港口；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Mainly
senses.definition: for the most part, more than any other thing
senses.definitionCN: 大部分情况下，超过任何其他事物
senses.example: The book is primarily about language.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书主要讲语言。
senses.why: The word ranks one element above the rest without denying that others exist.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把某一要素排在其余之上，却不否认其余要素存在。

senses.title: First in responsibility
senses.definition: used of the person or body with the main duty
senses.definitionCN: 用于承担主要职责的人或机构
senses.example: The committee is primarily responsible for safety.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会对安全负主要责任。
senses.why: Here the word concerns rank of obligation, not frequency or quantity.
senses.whyCN: 这里它说的是责任的等级，而不是频率或数量。

senses.title: Primarily because
senses.definition: used to name the main reason among several
senses.definitionCN: 用来在多个原因中指出主要那一个
senses.example: He resigned primarily because of ill health.
senses.exampleCN: 他辞职主要是因为健康不佳。
senses.why: The causal pattern admits other reasons while naming the dominant one.
senses.whyCN: 这一因果句式承认还有其他原因，同时点出主导原因。

senses.title: Primarily for a purpose
senses.definition: of a thing, intended first of all for one use
senses.definitionCN: 指某物的首要用途
senses.example: The land is used primarily for farming.
senses.exampleCN: 这片土地主要用于耕作。
senses.why: The word identifies the main function, leaving other uses as secondary.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指出主要功能，把其他用途留作次要。

senses.title: Primarily designed to
senses.definition: used before a verb of design or purpose to state the main aim
senses.definitionCN: 放在设计或目的动词前，说明主要目标
senses.example: The tool is primarily designed to cut wood.
senses.exampleCN: 这件工具的首要设计目的是切木头。
senses.why: Technical descriptions use the word to separate the intended function from incidental ones.
senses.whyCN: 技术说明用它把预期功能与附带功能分开。

senses.title: Primarily aimed at
senses.definition: of a course or product, intended mainly for one group
senses.definitionCN: 指课程或产品主要面向某一群体
senses.example: The programme is primarily aimed at beginners.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目主要面向初学者。
senses.why: The pattern states the target audience and implies that others are not the main concern.
senses.whyCN: 这一句式说明目标受众，并暗示其他人不是主要考虑。

senses.title: Formal register for mainly
senses.definition: in formal prose, a heavier alternative to mainly
senses.definitionCN: 在正式散文中，作为「主要」的较重替代
senses.example: The decline is primarily due to changes in demand.
senses.exampleCN: 这一下降主要归因于需求变化。
senses.why: Formal writing prefers the word when the claim carries weight in an argument.
senses.whyCN: 当论断在论证中有分量时，正式文字更偏爱这个词。

senses.title: Primarily concerned with
senses.definition: used of a field or text, focused on one subject above others
senses.definitionCN: 指某领域或文本把某一主题置于其他之上
senses.example: The chapter is primarily concerned with ethics.
senses.exampleCN: 这一章主要关注伦理问题。
senses.why: The phrase describes the centre of attention, often in academic summaries.
senses.whyCN: 这一短语描述注意力的中心，常用于学术摘要。

intro.en: Primarily comes from the Latin adjective for first in rank, through English primary, plus the adverb suffix. The direct source is clear; only the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个副词来自拉丁语「第一等级」的形容词，经英语形容词「首要的」，再加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: The adjective primus means first in order or rank.
items.cn: 形容词意为「在次序或等级上第一的」。

items.en: The adjective primarius means of the first rank or chief.
items.cn: 形容词意为「第一等级的、首要的」。

items.en: English primary comes through French and means first in importance as well as first in order.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入，既指次序最先，也指重要性居首。

items.en: The adverb adds the usual suffix; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 副词加常见后缀；英语首见年代为约数。

items.en: Modern usage ranks importance and purpose rather than strict temporal order.
items.cn: 现代用法排的是重要性与目的，而不是严格的时间先后。

items.en: The adverb settles in formal and technical prose as a stronger mainly.
items.cn: 这个副词在正式与技术散文中定型，语气比「主要地」更重。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin first-rank family; the second group contrasts main importance with leading rank or plain majority.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「第一等级」词族；第二组对照「主要重要性」与「首领地位」或「单纯多数」。

entries.definition: First in importance or order; the adjective behind the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 在重要性或次序上第一的；副词的形容词基形。

entries.definition: The state of being first in rank or authority.
entries.definitionCN: 在等级或权威上居首的状态。

entries.definition: First in quality or importance; also the period of greatest strength.
entries.definitionCN: 在质量或重要性上居首；也指最强盛的时期。

entries.definition: Belonging to the earliest or most basic level.
entries.definitionCN: 属于最早或最基础层面的。

entries.definition: For the most part; the plainer everyday counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 大部分情况下；更朴素的日常对应词。

entries.definition: Above all others, often ranking rather than measuring.
entries.definitionCN: 超过其他一切，常偏重等级而非数量。

entries.definition: To a great extent, often of proportions.
entries.definitionCN: 在很大程度上，常指比例。

entries.definition: Chiefly, with a heavier formal and institutional tone.
entries.definitionCN: 主要地，带更重的正式与机构语气。

entries.definition: More than everything else, with clear ranking.
entries.definitionCN: 超过其他一切，带明确的排序。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real first-rank family and the real split between main importance and leading rank.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「第一等级」词族，并区分「主要重要性」与「首领地位」。

normal.en: The root means first, so the word puts one item at the front of the line.
normal.cn: 词根意为「第一」，所以它把某一项排到队伍最前。

normal.en: Primarily responsible is about duty, not frequency.
normal.cn: 「负主要责任」说的是职责，不是频率。

normal.en: Primarily because names the leading reason and lets the others stand behind it.
normal.cn: 「主要因为」点出主导原因，让其他原因站在后面。

normal.en: Primarily aimed at identifies the audience the maker had in mind.
normal.cn: 「主要面向」指明制作者心里的受众。

normal.en: Formal prose uses it where mainly would sound too light for the claim.
normal.cn: 正式散文用它，因为「主要」对这份论断来说太轻。

abstract.en: Main importance is a ranking, and a ranking is a decision about what comes first.
abstract.cn: 主要性是一种排序，而排序就是决定什么排在最前。

abstract.en: A main door does not make the side doors unreal; it only decides where visitors enter.
abstract.cn: 正门并不让侧门变得不存在，它只决定客人从哪里进。

abstract.en: The word is a quiet way of saying that one reason outranks the rest.
abstract.cn: 这个词是安静地说：有一个理由压过其余。

examples.en: The region is primarily agricultural.
examples.cn: 这个地区主要从事农业。

examples.en: The delay was primarily caused by the weather.
examples.cn: 延误主要是天气造成的。

examples.en: The course is primarily intended for new staff.
examples.cn: 这门课程主要面向新员工。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普赖么瑞利」——排在第一排，主要就它

root: 拉丁语形容词「第一的」构成「第一等级的、首要的」，英语经法语借入形容词「主要的」，再加副词后缀。直接来源清楚，只有英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses separate main importance, first responsibility, leading reason, main purpose, primary design aim, target audience, formal register and academic focus.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分开处理主要重要性、首要责任、主导原因、主要用途、首要设计目的、目标受众、正式语域，以及学术关注点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the front door of a house, with several smaller side doors beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一栋房子的正门，旁边还有几扇小侧门。

branches.en: THE MAIN ELEMENT: more than any other thing.
branches.cn: 主要要素：超过任何其他事物。

branches.en: THE LEADING CLAIM: first responsibility and the dominant reason.
branches.cn: 领先的主张：首要责任与主导原因。

branches.en: THE INTENDED USE: main function and primary design aim.
branches.cn: 预期用途：主要功能与首要设计目的。

branches.en: THE AUDIENCE: the group the thing is mainly for.
branches.cn: 受众：该事物主要面向的群体。

branches.en: THE FORMAL CENTRE: heavier register and the focus of a field or text.
branches.cn: 正式中心：更重的语域，以及领域或文本的关注点。

intro.en: Primarily is a Latin first-adjective, its rank adjective, an English adjective and an English adverb suffix.
intro.cn: 这个副词由拉丁语「第一」形容词、表等级的形容词、英语形容词与英语副词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The first word builds an adjective of first rank, and English draws primary, primacy and prime from the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 表示「第一」的词构成「第一等级」的形容词，英语从同一词干取得「主要的」「首要地位」与「首要的」。

items.example: The adjective is the simple ranking word behind the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是词族背后最简单的排序词。

items.example: The suffix builds an adjective of rank.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表等级的形容词。

items.example: The adjective names those who stand at the head.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词指站在最前面的人。

items.example: English keeps both the ranking and the early-stage senses.
items.exampleCN: 英语同时保留「排序」与「早期阶段」两条义。

items.example: The noun names the position rather than the quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名位置，而不是性质。

items.example: The short form covers both rank and peak time.
items.exampleCN: 短形式同时覆盖等级与巅峰时期。

items.example: Another branch stresses earliness rather than rank.
items.exampleCN: 另一分支强调「最早」，而不是等级。

items.example: The suffix turns primary into a ranking adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成排序副词。

items.example: The adverb ranks importance in a whole statement.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词在整句范围内排定重要性。

definition_en: easy to see, hear or notice, or clearly different from something else
core_image: 两条并排的白线，中间留着一道谁也不碰谁的缝
scene: 白线画得很实，边缘一点也不含糊。 The two plans are distinct in almost every detail.
sceneCN: 这里 distinct 指「截然不同的」（第 2 个义项：彼此界限分明）；句意是这两个方案几乎每个细节都不同。

senses.title: Clear to the senses
senses.definition: easy to see, hear or notice, leaving no doubt
senses.definitionCN: 容易看见、听见或察觉，没有含糊
senses.example: There was a distinct smell of smoke.
senses.exampleCN: 有一股明显的烟味。
senses.why: A clear edge is what lets the eye rest on a thing.
senses.whyCN: 边缘清楚，眼睛才停得住。

senses.title: Clearly different
senses.definition: clearly separate and not the same as another thing
senses.definitionCN: 彼此分明，与另一物并不相同
senses.example: The two styles are distinct from each other.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种风格彼此截然不同。
senses.why: Two things stand apart only where one line is drawn between them.
senses.whyCN: 两样东西只有被一条线隔开，才显得分得清。

intro.en: Distinct is Latin distinctus, the past participle of distinguere, to separate, built on dis- and stinguere, to prick.
intro.cn: distinct 是拉丁语 distinctus，来自 distinguere（分开），由 dis- 与 stinguere（刺）构成，本义是刺出记号加以区分。

items.en: Stinguere meant to prick or mark with a point.
items.cn: stinguere 指用尖物刺或做记号。

items.en: Dis- pulled the marked pieces away from each other.
items.cn: dis- 把做过记号的几块分开。

items.en: Distinctus described what stood marked and separate.
items.cn: distinctus 描述被标记并分开放置的东西。

items.en: English used it for things clearly seen apart.
items.cn: 英语用它说清楚分得开的东西。

items.en: The sense of plain and unmistakable grew.
items.cn: 后来「明白无误」的意思壮大起来。

items.en: A distinct sound is both clear and unlike the rest.
items.cn: 今天 a distinct sound 既清楚又与众不同。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the stinguere stem, while the meaning group leans on clear edges and plain difference.
note.cn: 形近组共享 stinguere 这段词干，近义组则围绕清楚的边界与明显的差别。

entries.definition: to see or show a difference
entries.definitionCN: 看出或说明差别

entries.definition: a difference, or high quality
entries.definitionCN: 差别，或卓越

entries.definition: in a clear and unmistakable way
entries.definitionCN: 清楚而不含糊地

entries.definition: easy to see or understand
entries.definitionCN: 容易看见或理解

entries.definition: not joined or not the same
entries.definitionCN: 分开的或不相同的

entries.definition: so plain that no one doubts it
entries.definitionCN: 明显得无人怀疑

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a sharp white line and end with two things that share no edge.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一道利落的白线开始，落到两样连边都不碰的东西。

normal.en: Dis- plus stinguere: a mark is pricked, so the two are kept apart.
normal.cn: dis 加 stinguere，刺出一道记号，两者就分开了。

normal.en: The bell gave a distinct ring across the yard.
normal.cn: 铃声在院子里响得格外清楚。

normal.en: Coffee and tea have distinct smells once you pause.
normal.cn: 停下来一闻，咖啡和茶的气味截然不同。

normal.en: Keep the two files distinct, or the proof is lost.
normal.cn: 把两份文件分开，否则证据就乱了。

normal.en: Her voice was distinct even at the back of the hall.
normal.cn: 即便在大厅后排，她的声音也很清楚。

abstract.en: Picture two white lines with a clean gap between them.
abstract.cn: 想象两条白线中间留着一道干净的缝。

abstract.en: Picture a knife cutting a sheet into two neat halves.
abstract.cn: 想象一刀把纸裁成整齐的两半。

abstract.en: Picture a mark pricked into a card to tell one from another.
abstract.cn: 想象在卡片上刺一个记号，用来认出彼此。

examples.en: There is a distinct difference between the two roads.
examples.cn: 这两条路之间有明显的区别。

examples.en: Each district keeps a distinct local accent.
examples.cn: 每个区都保留着自己独特的口音。

examples.en: The outline was distinct against the pale sky.
examples.cn: 轮廓在淡色的天空下很清楚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 distinct 记成「刺出记号」：dis 表示分开，stinct 来自刺，刺出一个记号，两样东西就看得出不同，也显得清楚。

root: 源自拉丁语 distinguere（分开），词干 stinguere 意为用尖物刺、做记号，加 dis- 表示分开。本义是刺出标记把东西区别开，因此既指界限分明、彼此不同，也指轮廓清楚、毫不含糊。

sensesIntro.en: From a mark cut to keep two things apart to an edge the eye can follow without doubt.
sensesIntro.cn: 从刺下的一道区分记号，到眼睛毫不迟疑就能跟住的边线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two white lines side by side with a clean gap that neither crosses.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条并排的白线，中间一道谁也不越过的缝。

branches.en: The first sense is clearness to the eye or ear.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是眼睛或耳朵感到的清楚。

branches.en: The second sense is clearness between two things.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是两样东西之间的分明。

branches.en: Both senses depend on an edge that can be traced.
branches.cn: 两个义项都依赖一条能描出来的边。

branches.en: Both refuse the blur that mixes one thing into another.
branches.cn: 两个义项都拒绝把一物混成另一物的模糊。

branches.en: Only the second sense needs a second thing to compare.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项需要另一样东西来对照。

intro.en: Distinct sits in the stinguere family, where one pricked mark gives several words for separating and for clearness.
intro.cn: distinct 属于 stinguere 一族，一道刺出的记号，生出一串表示分开与清楚的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin stinguere, to prick, gives distinct and distinguish; dis- keeps the marked pieces apart.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stinguere（刺）给出 distinct 与 distinguish，前缀 dis- 让做过记号的几块保持分开。

items.example: A distinct line divides the fields.
items.exampleCN: 一条清楚的分界线隔开两块田。

definition_en: the act of using up fuel, food, energy or time, or the amount that is used
core_image: 水表数字不断跳动，一格一格往上走
scene: 工厂的用电数字每个季度都在往上爬。 Energy consumption rose sharply last winter.
sceneCN: 这里 consumption 指「消耗量」（第 1 个义项：实际用掉的能源或物资数量）；句意是去年冬天能源消耗量急剧上升。

senses.title: The amount used
senses.definition: the measured amount of fuel, food or energy that is used
senses.definitionCN: 被用掉的燃料、食物或能量的计量数值
senses.example: Fuel consumption fell after the new engine arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 换了新发动机后油耗下降了。
senses.why: What cannot be seen can still be counted on a meter.
senses.whyCN: 看不见的东西，也能在表上被数清。

senses.title: Buying and using
senses.definition: the economic activity of buying and using goods and services
senses.definitionCN: 购买并使用商品与服务的经济活动
senses.example: Household consumption drives half the economy.
senses.exampleCN: 家庭消费支撑着经济的一半。
senses.why: An economy is a circle, and spending keeps it turning.
senses.whyCN: 经济是一个圆圈，花销让它转起来。

senses.title: A wasting illness
senses.definition: an old name for tuberculosis, a disease that wastes the body away
senses.definitionCN: 肺结核的旧称，一种使身体日渐消瘦的病
senses.example: In the last century, consumption was often fatal.
senses.exampleCN: 在上个世纪，痨病常常致命。
senses.why: A disease that consumes the body borrowed the same word.
senses.whyCN: 一种把身体耗掉的病，借用了同一个词。

intro.en: Consumption comes from Latin consumptio, a using up, from consumere, to take completely.
intro.cn: consumption 来自拉丁语 consumptio，意为用尽，源自 consumere（彻底取走）。

items.en: Sumere meant to take, and consumere meant to take completely.
items.cn: sumere 意为拿取，consumere 意为彻底取走。

items.en: Consumptio named the act of using something up.
items.cn: consumptio 指把东西用掉的行为。

items.en: Medical writers used it for a body wasting away.
items.cn: 医学作者用它指身体日渐消瘦。

items.en: French consumption carried both the spending and the illness senses.
items.cn: 法语中的这个词同时带有耗费与疾病两层意思。

items.en: English consumption first meant the using up of things.
items.cn: 英语 consumption 最初指物品被用尽。

items.en: Economics made it the standard term for spending on goods.
items.cn: 经济学使它成为商品花销的标准术语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin take base sumpt-, and the meaning group names other words for the using of resources.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语拿取词基 sumpt-，近义组列出其他表示资源使用的词。

entries.definition: to use up fuel, food or time
entries.definitionCN: 消耗；用尽

entries.definition: a person who buys goods or services
entries.definitionCN: 消费者

entries.definition: something accepted as true without proof
entries.definitionCN: 假定；设想

entries.definition: the act of putting something to a purpose
entries.definitionCN: 使用；用途

entries.definition: the amount of something that is used

entries.definition: money or energy that is spent
entries.definitionCN: 支出；耗费

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a meter climbing, then move to a family filling a cart and to an old illness that empties a body.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从往上爬的计量表开始，再到把购物车装满的一家人，最后到一种把身体掏空的旧病。

normal.en: Consumption is consume turned into a noun you can measure.
normal.cn: consumption 是 consume 变成可以测量的名词。

normal.en: A meter that keeps climbing is consumption made visible.
normal.cn: 一只不断往上爬的表，就是把消耗变得看得见。

normal.en: Every cart leaving a shop adds to consumption.
normal.cn: 每一辆推出店门的购物车，都在给消费加数。

normal.en: Fuel consumption is a number a driver can lower.
normal.cn: 油耗是司机能压低的一个数字。

normal.en: What is consumed today is gone tomorrow.
normal.cn: 今天被消耗掉的东西，明天就没有了。

abstract.en: Picture digits turning over on a water meter.
abstract.cn: 想象水表上的数字一格格翻过去。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of receipts growing on a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上的小票越堆越高。

abstract.en: Picture a candle burning shorter every hour.
abstract.cn: 想象一根蜡烛每小时都短一截。

examples.en: Water consumption doubles in the hot months.
examples.cn: 炎热月份的用水量会翻倍。

examples.en: The government wants to cut energy consumption by a third.
examples.cn: 政府想把能源消耗削减三分之一。

examples.en: Rising consumption usually means a stronger economy.
examples.cn: 消费上升通常意味着经济更强。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 consumption 记成 consume（消耗）加 ption（名词）：把东西彻底用掉这件事，就是消耗，也用来说消耗量。

root: 源自拉丁语 consumptio（用尽），词根 consumere 由 com（彻底）与 sumere（拿取）构成，后指消耗量、消费与旧时所说痨病。

sensesIntro.en: From digits on a meter, to the spending of a whole economy, and at last to an old name for a wasting disease.
sensesIntro.cn: 从表上的数字，到整个经济的花销，最后到一种消耗身体的旧病名称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a meter whose digits keep climbing upward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只数字不断向上爬的计量表。

branches.en: The first sense is a figure you can read and compare.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是能读出来、能比较的数字。

branches.en: The second sense is the whole economy's habit of buying.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是整个经济的购买习惯。

branches.en: The third sense is a body using itself up.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是一个身体把自己耗掉。

branches.en: Both senses track how much passes from shelf to use.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在追踪有多少东西从货架走到使用。

branches.en: A meter and a disease both record a steady loss.
branches.cn: 计量表与疾病都记录着持续的减少。

intro.en: Consumption is built on Latin com-, completely, plus sumere, to take, with the noun ending -ption.
intro.cn: consumption 由拉丁语 com-（彻底）、sumere（拿取）与名词词尾 -ption 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin take base sumpt- also appears in assumption, resumption and presumption.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的拿取词基 sumpt- 也出现在 assumption、resumption 与 presumption 中。
