to take something until it is gone
items.example: The old boiler consumes too much gas.

items.meaning: a person who buys and uses goods
items.exampleCN: 消费者想要更低的价格。

items.example: The plan rests on a false assumption.
items.exampleCN: 这个计划建立在一个错误假定上。

items.example: The resumption of talks was welcome.

items.meaning: to place one thing under a larger class
items.meaningCN: 把一物归入更大的类别
items.example: The term subsumes many local names.
items.exampleCN: 这个术语涵盖了许多地方名称。

definition_zh: 最初的；开始的；首字母；姓名缩写；用首字母签署
definition_en: belonging to the beginning, or the first letter of a word or name
core_image: 一本书的第一页第一行，第一个字母被放大成金色花纹，后面的一切都从它开始
scene: 档案室里，编辑用笔圈出每份签名开头的那个字母。 The editor circled the initial letter of each name in the document.
sceneCN: 这里 initials 是「姓名首字母缩写」（第 3 个义项：用名字开头的字母代表全名）；句意：在这张表上写下你的姓名缩写就行。画面里有表格、笔和圈出的字母。

pos.zh: 首字母；姓名缩写；装饰性首字母

senses.title: At the start: the first moment
senses.titleCN: 最初的：时间上的第一步
senses.definition: happening at the beginning; first in a series
senses.definitionCN: 发生在开始时的；一系列中的第一个
senses.example: The initial results look promising.
senses.exampleCN: 初步结果看起来很有希望。
senses.why: The adjective is recorded from the 1520s as 'of or pertaining to a beginning'. Latin initialis came from initium 'a beginning', literally 'a going in' — the first step into something.
senses.whyCN: 形容词记录于 16 世纪 20 年代，意为“与开始有关的”。拉丁语 initialis 来自 initium“开始”，字面是“一次走入”——踏进某事的第一步。

senses.title: The first letter: where a word steps in
senses.titleCN: 首字母：一个词进门的地方
senses.definition: the first letter of a word or name
senses.definitionCN: 单词或姓名的第一个字母
senses.example: The poem's initials are decorated in gold.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗的首字母用金色装饰。
senses.why: The noun is recorded from the 1620s, shortened from the adjective in the specialized phrase 'initial letter'. A letter standing at the start of a word takes the name of the start itself.
senses.whyCN: 名词记录于 17 世纪 20 年代，是由短语 initial letter“开头的字母”中形容词的专指用法而来。站在一个词开头的字母，就直接借用了“开头”这个名字。

senses.title: Initials: several beginnings as one name
senses.titleCN: 姓名缩写：几个开头合成一个名字
senses.definition: the first letters of a person's names, used together to stand for the full name
senses.definitionCN: 一个人各名字的首字母合在一起，代表全名
senses.example: Please write your initials beside each correction.
senses.exampleCN: 请在每处修改旁写上你的姓名缩写。
senses.why: Once a single initial marks a word, the set of such letters can mark a whole name. The plural initials turns several beginnings into a compact signature.
senses.whyCN: 既然一个 initial 能标记一个词的开头，那么一组这样的字母就能标记整个姓名。复数 initials 把好几个“开头”压成一个紧凑的签名。

senses.title: To initial: sign with the first letters
senses.titleCN: 签首字母：用开头的字母代替签名
senses.definition: to mark or sign something with one's initials
senses.definitionCN: 用自己的姓名首字母标记或签署某物
senses.example: He initialed every page of the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 他在合同的每一页上签了姓名首字母。
senses.why: The verb is recorded from 1837, formed directly from the noun: to put the first letters where a full signature would go, a quick legal mark.
senses.whyCN: 动词记录于 1837 年，直接由名词构成：在本该写全名的地方写下开头的字母，是一种快捷的法律标记。

senses.title: At the front: a matter of position
senses.titleCN: 词首的、句首的：说的是位置而非时间
senses.definition: standing at the beginning of a word, sentence, or line
senses.definitionCN: 位于单词、句子或诗行的开头
senses.example: An initial consonant often carries the stress in English words.
senses.exampleCN: 英语单词的词首辅音常常承载重音。
senses.why: The 1620s adjective also meant 'standing at the beginning of a word, sentence, etc.' Here initial names a position, not a time: whatever occupies the front slot is initial.
senses.whyCN: 17 世纪 20 年代的形容词也指“位于词、句的开头”。这里 initial 命名的是位置而不是时间：占据最前面那个位置的，就是 initial。

senses.title: Initial sound: the consonant at the gate
senses.titleCN: 声母：守在音节门口的那个音
senses.definition: in phonetics, the sound or consonant at the start of a syllable
senses.definitionCN: 语音学上，音节开头的音或辅音
senses.example: Mandarin syllables are analysed as an initial and a final.
senses.exampleCN: 普通话的音节被分析为声母和韵母两部分。
senses.why: Phonology borrowed the positional sense: the initial is the consonant that opens a syllable, the part that stands at the gate before the vowel.
senses.whyCN: 音系学借走了那个位置义：声母是打开一个音节的那个辅音，是在韵母之前守在门口的部分。

senses.title: Early stage: the first, faint signs
senses.titleCN: 初期的：最早、最轻的那些迹象
senses.definition: early in a process, before later stages develop
senses.definitionCN: 处于过程的早期，后阶段尚未展开
senses.example: Initial symptoms of the disease are easy to miss.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病的初期症状很容易被忽略。
senses.why: From 'belonging to a beginning', medicine takes initial for the first, often faint stage of an illness. The later stages exist, but this is what shows at the door.
senses.whyCN: 医学从“属于开头”这一层取用 initial，指疾病最初、往往很轻的阶段。后面的阶段当然存在，但这一刻在门口露面的只是它。

senses.title: Starting setting: the value before change
senses.titleCN: 初始设置：改变之前的值
senses.definition: in computing and mathematics, the value or setting that exists at the start of a process
senses.definitionCN: 计算机或数学中，过程开始时就存在的值或设置
senses.example: You can restore the program to its initial settings.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以把程序恢复到初始设置。
senses.why: Modern technical use extends 'at the beginning' to a state before any change: initial conditions, initial settings. The word names the baseline from which a process runs.
senses.whyCN: 现代技术用法把“在开头”延伸到“任何改变之前的状态”：初始条件、初始设置。这个词命名的是一个过程启动时所依据的基线。

senses.title: The illuminated initial: a letter turned into a picture
senses.titleCN: 装饰首字母：被画成一幅画的那个字母
senses.definition: a large decorated letter at the start of a chapter in an old manuscript or printed book
senses.definitionCN: 古代手抄本或印本中，章节开头的大型装饰字母
senses.example: The illuminated initial shows a knight on horseback.
senses.exampleCN: 那个装饰首字母画着一位骑马的骑士。
senses.why: Medieval scribes enlarged the first letter of a chapter into a picture. The decorated initial is sense 02 given space and gold, marking where the text begins.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪抄写员把一章的第一个字母放大成一幅画。装饰首字母就是把第 2 义给了空间和金色，标记正文从哪里开始。

intro.en: Initial is built on the Latin verb inire 'to go into'. A beginning is literally a going in: one crosses a threshold, and the first letter of a word or name stands at that threshold.
intro.cn: initial 建在拉丁动词 inire“走进去”上。“开始”字面上就是“走进”：人跨过一道门槛，而单词或姓名的第一个字母就站在那道门槛上。

items.en: Inire meant 'to go into, enter upon, begin', from in- 'into' plus ire 'to go'. The deeper PIE root *ei- 'to go' is a reconstruction, so that step is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: inire 意为“走入、着手、开始”，由 in-“进入”加 ire“走”构成。更深的印欧语词根 *ei-“走”是重构形式，因此那一层标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: Initium meant 'a beginning, a commencement; an entrance, a going in'. It is a noun use of the neuter past participle of inire, so the word carries the image of having stepped inside.
items.cn: initium 意为“开始、开端；入口、一次走入”。它是 inire 中性过去分词的名词化用法，所以这个词自带“已经跨进去”的画面。

items.en: Initialis meant 'initial, incipient, of the beginning', derived from initium. Latin gave the adjective to French and to English.
items.cn: initialis 意为“开头的、初期的、属于开始的”，由 initium 派生。拉丁语把这个形容词传给了法语和英语。

items.en: The adjective is recorded as 'of or pertaining to a beginning', borrowed from French initial or directly from Latin initialis.
items.cn: 形容词记录为“与开始有关的”，借自法语 initial，或直接来自拉丁语 initialis。

items.en: The noun appears as 'initial letter of a name or surname', from a specialized use of the adjective meaning 'standing at the beginning of a word, sentence, etc.'
items.cn: 名词出现，意为“姓名或姓氏的首字母”，来自形容词“位于词、句开头”的专指用法。

items.en: The verb 'to mark or sign with initials' is recorded from 1837, formed from the noun. Related forms are initialed and initialing in American spelling.
items.cn: 动词“用首字母标记或签署”记录于 1837 年，由名词构成。美式拼写中相关形式为 initialed、initialing。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: the ability to act first without being told. It is initi- plus -ative, from the same initium.
entries.definitionCN: 主动性；率先行动的能力。它是 initi- 加 -ative，同出 initium。

entries.definition: at first; at the beginning. It is initial plus -ly and differs only in the ending.
entries.definitionCN: 起初；最初。它是 initial 加 -ly，只差词尾。

entries.definition: to begin something or bring someone into a group. It swaps the -ial ending for -iate.
entries.definitionCN: 开始；使入门。它把 -ial 词尾换成 -iate。

entries.definition: coming before all others in time or order. It is the plain English word for initial.
entries.definitionCN: 第一的；最先的。它是 initial 的朴素英语说法。

entries.definition: the first part or beginning of something. It stresses the moment a thing opens.
entries.definitionCN: 开头；开端。它强调事物“打开”的那一刻。

entries.definition: existing from the beginning, or first in a line. It points to origin rather than mere order.
entries.definitionCN: 最初的；原先的。它指向来源，而不只是顺序上的第一。

entries.definition: just beginning to appear or develop. It is more formal and often used of things not yet visible.
entries.definitionCN: 初期的；刚出现的。它更正式，常指尚未明显显现的事物。

entries.definition: done before the main event as preparation. It is initial in time, but serves something later.
entries.definitionCN: 初步的；预备的。它在时间上最前，但为后来的正事服务。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin inire 'to go in', initium 'a beginning', and the English family of initial, initiate, initiative.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 inire“走进”、initium“开始”，以及 initial、initiate、initiative 这一族英语词。

normal.en: initial = in- 'into' + ire 'to go': the first step is the one that goes in.
normal.cn: initial = in-“进入”+ ire“走”：第一步就是走进门的那一步。

normal.en: initium means 'a going in', so a beginning and an entrance are the same picture.
normal.cn: initium 意为“一次走入”，所以“开始”和“入口”是同一幅画。

normal.en: The initial letter stands at the doorway of a word, which is why the first letter is called an initial.
normal.cn: 首字母站在一个词的门槛上，所以第一个字母才叫 initial。

normal.en: Your initials are several doorways of your name compressed into one mark.
normal.cn: 你的姓名缩写，就是把你名字的几道门槛压成一个记号。

normal.en: initial settings are the values a program has before it has walked anywhere.
normal.cn: initial settings 是一个程序还没走到任何地方时的值。

abstract.en: The core is a threshold: whatever stands just inside the opening is initial.
abstract.cn: 核心是一道门槛：刚跨进门口的那一点，就是 initial。

abstract.en: The same word names a time, a letter, and a position, because all three are 'the front of something'.
abstract.cn: 同一个词命名时间、字母和位置，因为三者都是“某物的最前面”。

abstract.en: Beginning and entering are one idea here: to begin is to step through a door.
abstract.cn: 在这里，“开始”与“进入”是同一个念头：开始就是跨过一道门。

examples.en: The initial estimate was far too low.
examples.cn: 最初的估算远远偏低。

examples.en: Her initials are written in gold on the cover.
examples.cn: 她的姓名首字母用金色写在封面上。

examples.en: The initial stage of the project lasted six months.
examples.cn: 项目的初始阶段持续了六个月。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（进入）+ it（go 走）——刚走进门口的那一步 → initial 最初的；首字母

root: 源自拉丁语 initium“开始、进入”，由 inire“走进、开始”而来（in-“进入”+ ire“走”）；核心是“刚跨进门的那一步”，故引申为“最初的”与“首字母”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses built on one threshold: the first moment, the first letter, the letters that sign a name, the front position, the early stage, and the baseline before any change.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都建在一道门槛上：最初的时刻、第一个字母、签名字母、最前面的位置、早期阶段，以及任何改变之前的基线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a threshold; whatever stands at the opening is initial.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道门槛；站在门口的一切都是 initial。

branches.en: THE FIRST MOMENT: what happens at the beginning, and the early stage of an illness.
branches.cn: 最初的时刻：开头发生的事，以及疾病的早期阶段。

branches.en: THE FIRST LETTER: the opening letter of a word, and its decorated manuscript form.
branches.cn: 第一个字母：词的开头字母，以及它在手抄本里的装饰形态。

branches.en: THE COMPACT SIGNATURE: initials standing for a name, and the act of signing with them.
branches.cn: 紧凑的签名：代表姓名的首字母，以及用它们签署的动作。

branches.en: THE FRONT SLOT: a letter at the start of a word or sentence, and the initial sound of a syllable.
branches.cn: 最前面的位置：词或句首的字母，以及音节的词首音。

branches.en: THE STARTING STATE: the default value or condition before a process changes it.
branches.cn: 起始状态：过程改变它之前的默认值或条件。

intro.en: Initial is in- plus it- plus -ial. Its family shows the prefix in-, the root it- from ire 'to go', and the suffixes -ial, -ly, -iate, -ion, -ive, -or, -ism and -ize.
intro.cn: initial 是 in- 加 it- 再加 -ial。它的词族展示前缀 in-，来自 ire“走”的词根 it-，以及后缀 -ial、-ly、-iate、-ion、-ive、-or、-ism、-ize。

latinIntro.en: Latin inire 'to go into' gives initium 'a beginning' and initialis 'of the beginning'. The same root produces initiate, initiation and initiative.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 inire“走入”给出 initium“开始”和 initialis“属于开始的”。同一个词根产生 initiate、initiation、initiative。

items.meaning: of the beginning; the first letter
items.meaningCN: 最初的；首字母（走进门的那一步）
items.example: Our initial plan was too ambitious.
items.exampleCN: 我们最初的计划过于宏大。

items.meaningCN: 起初；最初（-ly 副词后缀）
items.example: Initially, no one believed the story.
items.exampleCN: 起初没有人相信这个故事。

items.meaning: to begin; to bring someone into a practice
items.meaningCN: 开始；使入门（-iate 动词后缀）
items.example: They initiated a new health program.
items.exampleCN: 他们发起了一项新的健康计划。

items.meaning: the act of beginning or admitting a member
items.meaningCN: 开始；入会仪式（-ion 动作名词）
items.example: The club's initiation includes a short test.
items.exampleCN: 这个俱乐部的入会仪式包括一项小测试。

items.meaning: the power to act first; a new plan
items.example: She took the initiative and called the client.
items.exampleCN: 她主动打电话给了客户。

items.example: He was the initiator of the reform.
items.exampleCN: 他是这场改革的发起人。

items.meaning: a word formed from first letters, each sounded separately
items.example: FBI is an initialism, not an acronym.
items.exampleCN: FBI 是首字母缩略词，不是首字母拼音词。

items.meaning: to set a device or program to its starting state
items.example: The system initializes the drive on startup.
items.exampleCN: 系统在启动时会初始化该驱动器。

items.meaning: serving as an introduction or first rite
items.meaningCN: 入门的；起始的（-atory 形容词后缀）
items.example: The initiatory rite lasted three days.

items.meaning: not yet introduced to a group or body of knowledge
items.meaningCN: 未入门的；外行的（un- 否定 + -ed）
items.example: The lecture assumed no knowledge, so the uninitiated could follow.
items.exampleCN: 这场讲座假定听众零基础，所以外行也能听懂。

latinEntries.meaning: to go into, enter upon, begin

definition_zh: 投资；投入（时间精力）；授予（权力）
definition_en: to put money, time, or effort into something hoping for a return, or to formally give someone power or a right
core_image: 一笔钱被装进土里，等着日后长出更多
scene: 父亲把存折推到女儿面前，让她自己决定怎么用这笔学费之外的钱。 She decided to invest half of it in a small bakery.
sceneCN: 这里 invest 是「投资」（第 1 个义项：把钱投出去以求回报），句意为她决定把其中一半投进一家小面包店。画面里的物件：存折、桌面、台灯。

pos.zh: 动词：投资；投入；授予权力

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ment 构成，义为「投资；投资额」
由本词加 -or 构成，义为「投资者」
加前缀 di- 构成的反向词，义为「撤资；剥夺」
去掉 in- 的同源词，义为「背心；授予」

senses.title: Putting money to work
senses.definition: to put money into a business or asset in order to make a profit later
senses.definitionCN: 把钱放进企业或资产，指望日后获利
senses.example: They invested their savings in solar panels for the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把积蓄投在了屋顶的太阳能板上。
senses.why: Latin investire meant "to clothe", and money clothed in a venture was said to be invested.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 investire 意为「给穿衣」，钱被「穿」进一桩事业，就叫投了出去。

senses.title: Spending effort
senses.definition: to give time, energy, or attention to something because it matters
senses.definitionCN: 因为某事重要而付出时间、精力或注意力
senses.example: She invested three years in learning the violin.
senses.exampleCN: 她花了三年时间学小提琴。
senses.why: If money can be dressed in a project, so can effort: both are resources you part with.
senses.whyCN: 钱能披挂在一个项目上，力气也行：两者都是你交出去的资源。

senses.title: Giving formal power
senses.definition: to give someone the official right or power to act in a role
senses.definitionCN: 正式赋予某人在某职位上行动的权力
senses.example: The new mayor was invested with the authority to hire staff.
senses.exampleCN: 新市长被授予聘用员工的权力。
senses.why: The oldest sense is ceremonial: a robe was put on someone to show the office was now theirs.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是仪式性的：给别人穿上礼服，表示职位从此归他。

intro.en: Invest began as a word about clothes and ceremony long before it meant money.
intro.cn: invest 在表示钱之前，长期是个关于衣服与仪式的词。

items.en: The noun vestis meant "garment".
items.cn: 名词 vestis 意为「衣服」。

items.en: investire meant "to put a garment on someone".
items.cn: investire 意为「给人穿上衣服」。

items.en: The Church used it for dressing a person in the robes of an office.
items.cn: 教会用它表示给人穿上某职位的礼服。

items.en: Trade turned the idea of clothing into placing money in a venture.
items.cn: 商业把「穿衣」的想法转成了把钱放进一桩事业。

items.en: Banks and markets fixed the financial sense in everyday speech.
items.cn: 银行与市场把这一金融义固定进了日常语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the vest- stem; the near-meaning group holds words about putting resources in.
note.cn: 形近组共用 vest- 词干；近义组收表示投入资源的词。

entries.definition: A sleeveless garment worn under a jacket.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「背心」，同词根。

entries.definition: To sell off holdings or strip someone of power.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「撤资；剥夺」，反向词。

entries.definition: To create something new.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「发明」，拼写只差一个字母。

entries.definition: To provide money for a project.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「资助」，提供资金。

entries.definition: To give time or attention completely to something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「奉献」，强调全心全意。

entries.definition: To set money or resources aside for a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「拨出」，指分配。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move the word from a robe to a wallet.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把这个词从礼服挪到钱包。

normal.en: in- means in, and vest- means clothes.
normal.cn: in- 是「进入」，vest- 是「衣服」。

normal.en: Money is dressed in a project, so it is invested.
normal.cn: 钱被「穿」在项目上，所以叫投进去。

normal.en: What you put in is an investment.
normal.cn: 你放进去的那笔就叫 investment。

normal.en: The person who puts it in is an investor.
normal.cn: 放进去的人叫 investor。

normal.en: Dress effort in a cause and you invest in it too.
normal.cn: 把力气披挂在一件事上，也是 invest。

abstract.en: Investment is trust wearing a price tag.
abstract.cn: 投资是贴上价签的信任。

abstract.en: To invest is to plant and then leave the field alone.
abstract.cn: 投资是种下去，然后先别去动那块地。

abstract.en: Power, like money, is handed over by an act of dressing.
abstract.cn: 权力和钱一样，都靠一个「加衣」的动作交出去。

examples.en: The fund invests mainly in small farms.
examples.cn: 这只基金主要投资小型农场。

examples.en: He invested every spare hour in the repair of the boat.
examples.cn: 他把每一个空闲小时都投在了修船上。

examples.en: The board invested the director with full control of the budget.
examples.cn: 董事会授予这位主管完全的预算控制权。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（进去）+ vest（衣服）——把钱裹进项目里

root: 拉丁语 in「进入」+ vestis「衣服」→ investire「给穿衣」→ 中世纪拉丁语指授职 → 英语 invest 引申为「投资」。同族有 investment、investor、divest、vest。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: putting in money, putting in effort, and formally granting power.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：投入金钱、投入精力，以及正式授予权力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something valuable is handed over and dressed in a new role.
core.cn: 核心意象：有价值的东西被交出去，并披上一个新的身份。

branches.en: THE PURSE: money placed where it can grow.
branches.cn: 钱包这条线：放在能生长之处的钱。

branches.en: THE HOURS: time given to a craft or cause.
branches.cn: 时间这条线：给一门手艺或一件事的时间。

branches.en: THE ROBE: official authority put on a person.
branches.cn: 礼服这条线：披在某人身上的官方权力。

branches.en: THE RESOURCE: both senses part with something now for later.
branches.cn: 资源这条线：两个义项都是现在付出、以后收获。

branches.en: THE GRANT: both senses make a formal transfer of value.
branches.cn: 授予这条线：两个义项都完成一次正式的价值转移。

intro.en: Invest is in- "into" plus vestis "garment"; the robe may be worn by a man or by money.
intro.cn: invest 是 in-「进入」加 vestis「衣服」，穿上礼服的可能是人，也可能是钱。

latinIntro.en: Latin vestis, vestire and investire are all recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vestis、vestire 与 investire 均有记载。

items.example: The root names what is put on.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指被穿上的东西。

items.example: The verb is the family base.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一族的基座。

items.example: The bare stem still names a piece of clothing.
items.exampleCN: 光词干至今仍指一件衣服。

items.example: It builds divest, to strip away.

items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把方向反了过来。

definition_en: the quality of continuing to try despite difficulty, or the act of deciding something firmly
core_image: 桌下握紧的拳头，脸上却仍旧平静地看着前方
scene: 长跑最后一圈，她的双腿在抖，眼神却没有散。 Her determination carried her through the final mile.
sceneCN: 这里 determination 指「决心」（第 1 个义项：坚持到底的意志）；句意是她的决心带她跑完了最后一英里。

senses.title: Firmness of purpose
senses.definition: the quality of continuing to try even when something is difficult
senses.definitionCN: 即使困难也继续尝试的品质
senses.example: Her determination carried her through the final mile.
senses.exampleCN: 她的决心带她跑完了最后一英里。
senses.why: The legs were ready to stop; something above them refused.
senses.whyCN: 双腿已经准备停下，是更上面的什么东西不肯。

senses.title: A firm decision
senses.definition: a formal decision that settles a question for good
senses.definitionCN: 把某个问题彻底定下来的正式决定
senses.example: The committee reached a determination after two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会两小时后作出了决定。
senses.why: A matter is weighed once, then the scale is allowed to rest.
senses.whyCN: 事情称过一次，然后就让秤停下来。

senses.title: Working something out exactly
senses.definition: the act of finding out an amount or a cause precisely
senses.definitionCN: 精确查明某个数量或原因的行为
senses.example: The determination of the cause took several weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 查明原因花了几个星期。
senses.why: To determine is to put a boundary around an unknown.
senses.whyCN: 所谓确定，就是给一片未知画上边界。

intro.en: Determination comes from Latin determinare, to set a limit, built from de- and terminus, a boundary stone, and it passed through French.
intro.cn: determination 来自拉丁语 determinare（划定界限），由 de- 与 terminus（界石）构成，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Terminus meant a boundary stone, and determinare meant to set a limit.
items.cn: terminus 指界石，determinare 指划定界限。

items.en: The word also meant to settle a question by fixing its edges.
items.cn: 这个词也指把问题的边界钉死，从而把它了结。

items.en: French determination carried the sense of a settled decision.
items.cn: 法语 determination 带着「已经定下的决定」这层意思。

items.en: English used it for a legal ruling and for firmness of mind.
items.cn: 英语用它同时表示法律裁决与内心的坚定。

items.en: Science added the exact measurement of an amount or a cause.
items.cn: 科学又添上精确测定数量或原因这一用法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the termin stem, while the meaning group covers resolve, persistence and decisions.
note.cn: 形近组共用 termin 这个词干，近义组则覆盖决意、坚持与决定。

entries.definition: to decide or find out something firmly
entries.definitionCN: 坚定地决定或查明某事

entries.definition: having a strong wish to do something
entries.definitionCN: 怀着强烈意愿去做某事的

entries.definition: the end of a line or a building for travellers
entries.definitionCN: 线路的终点或旅客集散的建筑

entries.definition: a firm decision to do something
entries.definitionCN: 要做某事的坚定决定

entries.definition: the act of continuing despite difficulty
entries.definitionCN: 遇到困难仍继续下去

entries.definition: a choice that has been made
entries.definitionCN: 已经作出的选择

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a clenched fist under a desk and end with a boundary stone in a field.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从桌下攥紧的拳头开始，落到田野里的一块界石。

normal.en: Terminus is a boundary stone, so to determine is to mark where a thing ends.
normal.cn: terminus 是一块界石，所以 determine 就是标出某物到哪儿为止。

normal.en: Determination is a line you draw and then refuse to move.
normal.cn: 决心就是你画下一条线，然后拒绝挪动它。

normal.en: A firm decision is quiet; it has no need to shout.
normal.cn: 坚定的决定是安静的，它不必喊。

normal.en: The same word settles a debate and measures a cause.
normal.cn: 同一个词既了结争论，也测定原因。

normal.en: Where the stone stands, the argument stops.
normal.cn: 界石立在哪儿，争论就停在哪儿。

abstract.en: Picture a stone half sunk in wet grass.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石头半埋在湿草里。

abstract.en: Picture a fist opening slowly on a table.
abstract.cn: 想象一只拳头在桌面上慢慢松开。

abstract.en: Picture a scale arm settling at last.
abstract.cn: 想象天平的长臂终于稳住。

examples.en: Her determination carried her through the final mile.
examples.cn: 她的决心带她跑完了最后一英里。

examples.en: He spoke with quiet determination about the plan.
examples.cn: 他平静而坚定地谈起这个计划。

examples.en: The result was never really in doubt.
examples.cn: 结果其实从来没有悬念。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 determination 记成「地特米内神」：de 是定下，termin 是边界，把边界钉死，就是确定，也是决心。

root: 来自拉丁语 determinare，由 de-（加强）与 terminus（界石、边界）组成，经法语进入英语。本义是划定边界、把问题定死，后来引申为作出决定，又引申为内心的坚定与精确测定。

sensesIntro.en: From a will that will not bend, to a question closed for good, to an amount measured exactly.
sensesIntro.cn: 从不肯弯折的意志，到被彻底了结的问题，再到被精确测出的数量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boundary stone driven into the ground and a hand that will not move it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块界石被钉进地里，而有一只手不肯挪动它。

branches.en: The first sense is the will that keeps standing at the stone.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是始终守在界石旁的那股意志。

branches.en: The second sense is the moment the boundary closes a debate.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是边界把争论关上的那一刻。

branches.en: The third sense is the measuring that finds where the edge really is.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是找出边界究竟在哪里的测量。

branches.en: A settled decision and a steady will are the same line seen twice.
branches.cn: 已定的决定与稳定的意志，是同一条线被看了两次。

branches.en: To decide and to measure both put an end to vagueness.
branches.cn: 作决定与作测量，都在终结含糊。

intro.en: Determination has a family built on the Latin boundary stone and on the act of fixing a limit.
intro.cn: determination 有一族词，建在拉丁语的界石与「划界」这个动作上。

latinIntro.en: The base is terminus, a boundary, and de- plus -ation turn it into the act of setting limits.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是 terminus（边界），加上 de- 与 -ation，就成了划定界限这一行为。

items.exampleCN: 她的决心让所有人吃惊。

items.meaning: to decide or find out exactly
items.example: They will determine the cause soon.
items.exampleCN: 他们很快就会查明原因。

items.meaning: a factor that decides a result
items.exampleCN: 成本是主要的决定因素。

items.meaning: the belief that all events are fixed

items.example: The delay was of indeterminate length.
items.exampleCN: 这次延误的长短并不确定。

items.example: Determining the date took a week.

definition_zh: 政权；统治制度；管理体制；养生法；训练方案
definition_en: a government or system of ruling a country, or a planned way of living, eating, or training
core_image: 一整套按固定刻度运转的规程：国家用它统治，身体用它作息
scene: 铁栅门开了又关，喇叭里每天定点传出同样的通告。 Life under the old regime was strict and silent.
sceneCN: 这里 regime 是「政权；统治制度」（第 1 个义项：统治国家的一套体制）；句意：旧政权治下的生活严苛而沉默。场景要点：高墙、喇叭、整齐的脚步声。

pos.zh: 政权；统治制度；管理体制；养生法；训练方案

forms.label: 复数（多种体制、多个方案）

derivatives.zh: 同源近亲词，义为「养生法；疗程；作息制度」（更强调规则本身）
同源词，义为「团（军队编制）；纪律约束」（作动词指严格管束）
同前缀词，义为「地区的；区域的」（出自 regere 的领域概念）
同根动词，义为「管理；调节；管制」

senses.title: A government that rules
senses.definition: a government, especially one that rules in a particular or forceful way
senses.definitionCN: 一个政府，尤指以特定或强势方式执政的政府
senses.example: The old regime collapsed after weeks of protest.
senses.exampleCN: 旧政权在数周抗议后垮台。
senses.why: The Latin regere means 'to rule, guide straight': the regime is the hand on the reins of a country.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 regere 意为「统治、引直」：regime 就是握着一国缰绳的那只手。

senses.title: The system and style of rule
senses.definition: the method, system, or period during which a particular government or style of governing holds power
senses.definitionCN: 特定政府或执政方式掌权的方法、制度或时期
senses.example: Scholars still study the economic policies of that regime.
senses.exampleCN: 学者们仍在研究那个时期的各项经济政策。
senses.why: Ruling is not just holding power but steering it: the system of steering, like the run of a racehorse, takes the same name.
senses.whyCN: 统治不只是握权，更是驾驭：这套驾驭体系，如赛马的奔跑步法，用的是同一个名字。

senses.title: A managed system in an organization
senses.definition: a system of managing or controlling an organization, activity, or area
senses.definitionCN: 管理或控制某机构、活动或领域的体系
senses.example: The industry operates under a strict licensing regime.
senses.exampleCN: 该行业在严格的许可制度下运营。
senses.why: Any ruled domain is a little state: the same straightening hand governs prices, licences, or machines.
senses.whyCN: 任何被治理的领域都是一个小国：同一只「引直」之手管着价格、执照或机器。

senses.title: A planned routine for the body
senses.definition: a planned set of rules for diet, exercise, or medical treatment, followed regularly
senses.definitionCN: 为饮食、锻炼或治疗而制订、定期遵守的一套规则
senses.example: He follows a strict regime of swimming and stretching every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他每天早上严格执行游泳加拉伸的训练方案。
senses.why: The body, like the state, is ruled by a straightening hand: rules for eating and exercise hold the body to its line.
senses.whyCN: 身体如同国家，也由一只「引直」之手治理：饮食与锻炼的规则把身体保持在线上。

intro.en: Regime comes from French régime, from Latin regimen 'rule, guidance, steering', from regere 'to rule, to keep straight'. Latin regimen covered both the reins of a horse and the discipline of a body, and modern English has inherited the double use.
intro.cn: regime 来自法语 régime，上溯拉丁语 regimen「统治、指导、驾驭」，出自 regere「统治、保持笔直」。拉丁语 regimen 既指马的缰绳，也指身体的规训，现代英语继承了这双重用法。

items.en: The reconstructed root *h3reg- 'to move in a straight line, to direct' underlies Latin regere, English right, reckon and rich, all picture a straight guiding hand.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 *h3reg-「直线行进、引导」生成了拉丁语 regere 与英语 right、reckon、rich——都画着一只「引直」之手。

items.en: Regimen meant 'the act of steering, rule, discipline', used of government and of health rules alike; regere also gives regula 'a straight bar, rule'.
items.cn: regimen 意为「驾驭、统治、规训」，既用于政务也用于健康规则；regere 还派生 regula「直杆、规则」。

items.en: French régime carried both senses: the style of government and the ordered way of living, especially diet and discipline.
items.cn: 法语 régime 兼有两义：执政风格，以及有次序的生活方式，尤指饮食与规训。

items.en: The word enters English first as the diet-and-health sense; the political sense 'particular government' grows in the eighteenth century, often of foreign governments.
items.cn: 该词先以「饮食养生」义进入英语；「特定政府」的政治义在十八世纪成长，常指外国政权。

items.en: The political use becomes dominant in journalism, often with a critical flavour; the sense of any managed system, from taxes to training, spreads widely.
items.cn: 新闻语体中政治义渐成主导，常带批评色彩；从税收制度到训练计划，「任何受管体系」的用法广泛铺开。

note.en: The first group gathers the regere 'rule straight' family, where regimen and regiment share the same Latin shape with different fates. The second group compares the words for systems of rule.
note.cn: 第一组汇集 regere「引直统治」词族，regimen 与 regiment 同形异命。第二组比较「统治体系」类词。

entries.definition: a prescribed course of diet, exercise, or treatment. It stresses the rules; regime can name the rulers themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 规定的饮食、锻炼或疗程。它强调规则；regime 可指统治者本身。

entries.definition: a military unit of a thousand or so soldiers; as a verb, to control people too strictly. Same straightening root, pointed at soldiers.
entries.definitionCN: 约千人的军队编制单位；作动词指过度管束。同一「引直」词根，指向士兵。

entries.definition: to control by rules, keeping something working straight. The verb behind the regime.
entries.definitionCN: 用规则管制，使运转保持笔直。是 regime 背后的动词。

entries.definition: a person who rules in place of a monarch, as a child king's stand-in.
entries.definitionCN: 代君主执政的人，如幼年国王的替手。

entries.definition: a large area of land. The ruled district of the same root: what the straightening hand governs.
entries.definitionCN: 大片陆地。同一词根的「辖区」：被引直之手治理的地方。

entries.definition: the body that governs a country. Government is the neutral word; regime often implies judgement on how it rules.
entries.definitionCN: 治理国家的机构。government 是中性词；regime 常隐含对其执政方式的评判。

entries.definition: the executive part of a government, often named for its leader. It stresses running the machine, not the style of ruling.
entries.definitionCN: 政府的行政分支，常以其领导人命名。它强调运转机器，而非执政风格。

entries.definition: an organized set of rules or methods. System has no hand on the reins; regime always implies one.
entries.definitionCN: 有组织的规则或方法体系。system 没有握缰之手；regime 总是暗含一只。

entries.definition: a usual sequence of actions. Routine is what one drifts into; a regime is planned and imposed.
entries.definitionCN: 惯常的行为序列。routine 是自然养成的；regime 是被规划并强加的。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin regere 'to rule, keep straight', the family regimen, regiment, regulate and region, and the reins-in-hand picture.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 regere「统治、保持笔直」，词族 regimen、regiment、regulate、region，以及「手握缰绳」的图景。

normal.en: regere means to keep straight: a ruler keeps a country on the line, as reins keep a horse.
normal.cn: regere 意为「保持笔直」：统治者让国家走在线上，如同缰绳管住马。

normal.en: Regimen and regime are the same Latin word in two English rooms: one for rules, one for rulers.
normal.cn: regimen 与 regime 是同一个拉丁词住进英语的两间屋：一间放规则，一间放统治者。

normal.en: Regiment, the soldiers' unit, carries the same root: troops ruled into straight lines.
normal.cn: 军队编制 regiment 同根：士兵被治成笔直的队列。

normal.en: Region is the ground that is ruled: the governed area of the same word.
normal.cn: region 是被治理的土地：同一个词的「辖区」。

normal.en: Right and rich are distant cousins: straightness, correctness and power all grow from one root.
normal.cn: right 与 rich 是远亲：笔直、正确与权力都从同一个根上长出。

abstract.en: Picture reins tied to a whole country: whoever holds them runs the regime.
abstract.cn: 想象缰绳拴在整片国土上：谁握住它，谁就运行这个 regime。

abstract.en: A training regime is the country of your body, ruled for one hour at a time.
abstract.cn: 训练方案是你身体的小国，一次只统治一个小时。

abstract.en: Every regime draws straight lines first: through budgets, timetables and habits.
abstract.cn: 每个 regime 都先画直线：穿过预算、课表和习惯。

examples.en: The army took over and a military regime was installed.
examples.cn: 军队接管，一个军事政权建立了。

examples.en: Under the new tax regime, small firms pay less.
examples.cn: 在新税制下，小企业缴税更少。

examples.en: Her doctors designed a gentle regime of rest and medicine.
examples.cn: 医生们为她设计了一套温和的休养服药方案。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞吉姆」——瑞福天天按「日程表」执行统治般的作息 → regime 政权；管理体制；养生方案（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 regimen「统治、驾驭」（regere 引直、统治），核心是「握缰引直之手」，既指治国，也指治身。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of regime, one hand seen at two reins: the reins of a state, of an industry, and of one's own body.
sensesIntro.cn: regime 的四个义项是同一只手握着的几副缰绳：国家的、行业的，以及自己身体的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand holding reins, keeping what it rules on a straight line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只握着缰绳的手，把所治之物保持在线上。

chain: APPLY THE HAND TO THE BODY

branches.en: THE STATE: the government itself and the manner and period of its ruling.
branches.cn: 国家：政府本身及其执政的方式与时期。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: any managed domain — taxes, licences, factories — runs like a small state.
branches.cn: 体系：任何受管领域——税、执照、工厂——都像一个小国般运转。

branches.en: THE BODY: diet and training rules are the reins held over oneself.
branches.cn: 身体：饮食与训练规则是握在自己身上的缰绳。

branches.en: SCALE: the same straightening hand governs a country and a company's paperwork.
branches.cn: 尺度：同一只引直之手既治一国，也治一纸公文。

branches.en: TIME: both the style of rule and the daily routine run on a fixed schedule.
branches.cn: 时间：执政风格与日常作息都按固定节拍运转。

intro.en: Regime carries the Latin stem regere 'to rule, keep straight'. The family fills a page of English: regulate, regulator, regular, region, regent, regimen and regiment all descend from it.
intro.cn: regime 带有拉丁词干 regere「统治、保持笔直」。这个词族在英语中占满一页：regulate、regulator、regular、region、regent、regimen、regiment 都出自它。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is regimen 'steering, rule', from regere 'to keep straight, guide'. Regere also gives regula 'straight bar', the ancestor of rule and regular.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语源头是 regimen「驾驭、统治」，出自 regere「保持笔直、引导」。regere 还派生 regula「直杆」，即 rule 与 regular 的祖先。

items.meaning: a system of rule; a planned routine
items.meaningCN: 政权；体制；养生方案（regere 统治 + -men 结果名词）
items.exampleCN: 该政权收紧了新闻管控。

items.meaning: a prescribed course of diet or treatment
items.meaningCN: 养生法；疗程（强调规则本身）
items.example: Stick to the prescribed regimen for two weeks.
items.exampleCN: 遵医嘱的疗程坚持两周。

items.meaning: a military unit; to rule too strictly
items.meaningCN: 军团；过度管束（-ment 构成名词）
items.example: He hated being regimented even on holiday.
items.exampleCN: 即使在假期他也受不了被严格管制。

items.meaningCN: 管制；调节（regula 直杆 + -ate 动词）
items.exampleCN: 该机构负责食品安全监管。

items.meaning: a device or official that keeps a system steady
items.meaningCN: 调节器；监管者（-or 表示装置或人员）
items.example: The pressure regulator keeps the boiler safe.

items.meaning: following a rule; happening at even intervals
items.meaningCN: 规律的；定期的（regula 规则 + -ar）
items.example: He is a regular at that noodle shop.

items.meaning: a large governed area of land
items.meaningCN: 地区；区域（被治理的地域）
items.example: The region grows most of the country's tea.
items.exampleCN: 该地区出产全国大部分茶叶。

items.meaning: one who rules on a monarch's behalf
items.meaningCN: 摄政者（-ent 表示施动者）
items.example: The queen mother acted as regent for years.

items.meaning: an official rule; the act of controlling
items.meaningCN: 规章；管制（-ion 构成名词）

items.meaning: having the job of controlling by rules
items.meaningCN: 监管的；规章的（-ory 表示职能）
items.example: A regulatory body reviews the bank's accounts.
items.exampleCN: 监管机构审查银行账目。

latinEntries.meaning: to rule, to keep straight, to guide
